name: Reference adult body mass
notes: THE ROW HANDOVER SECTION 9 SAYS IS MISSING: 'body_mass is not a ledger row and is the largest un-modelled dimorphism'. It was a hard-coded 70.0 default on three function signatures. It is now one number in one place and the model scales to it. ASSUMED, NOT SOURCED, AND DELIBERATELY SO. 70 kg is the conventional reference adult and it is entered here as the value the code already used, so that promoting it to the ledger changes NOTHING - size_factor returns exactly 1.0 and every existing result is bit-identical. Dressing it in a citation at the same time as changing the model structure would have made two changes at once and left neither testable. THE SEXED PAIR IS THE NEXT STEP AND THE SOURCE IS ALREADY WHITELISTED. SOURCES.md admits ICRP Publication 89 (reference anatomical and physiological values) as tier A, and it carries reference adult masses by sex. That extraction is NOT done here and the numbers are NOT guessed at: per directive 1.5 a citation nobody opened is worse than an honest assumption. When it lands this row becomes a male/female pair under ADR 0014 and, because every extensive quantity in the model now scales through it, it will move the whole model for both sexes at once - which is exactly what the handover means by calling body mass the largest un-modelled dimorphism. WHAT SCALES THROUGH IT: see src/scaling.jl. Extensive quantities scale linearly, intensive ones do not. Linear-in-mass is exact for the volumes, which are already entered as mass fractions, and is an APPROXIMATION for GFR and cardiac output, which are conventionally normalised to body surface area and therefore grow sub-linearly with mass. Linear scaling OVERSTATES their population spread. Fixing that needs height, which this model does not carry. Recorded as debt rather than approximated with an unsourced allometric exponent. CLARIFIED 2026-08-27 WHEN THE NHANES EXTRACTION LANDED. This row is the mass at which this ledger's EXTENSIVE CONSTANTS ARE STATED - GFR 180 L/day, CO 7200 mL/min, blood volume 5.0 L are textbook values for a roughly 70 kg, 1.73 m2 adult - so it is a normalisation convention belonging to those sources, NOT a claim about how much people weigh. It stays `both` and stays 70.0. The claim about people is BF.BODY_MASS.TYPICAL, which IS a male/female pair (90.3 / 77.9 kg, NHANES 2021-2023). Moving THIS row to a population mean would rescale every extensive constant against a denominator its own sources never used, turning GFR into 232 L/day by arithmetic rather than by measurement. The two rows are different quantities and ADR 0014 applies to each separately. || ROUNDED 2026-09-09 TO MEASUREMENT PRECISION at the owner's instruction. Nothing physiological in this model is measured to more than four significant figures, and trailing zeros on a whole number read as precision that is not there. The discarded digits were floating-point residue from the derivation, not information. Directive 1.13.

name: Typical adult body mass, population mean
citation: Fryar CD, Gu Q, Afful J, Carroll MD, Ogden CL. Anthropometric Reference Data for Children and Adults: United States, August 2021-August 2023. Vital and Health Statistics Series 3, No. 50. Atlanta (GA): National Center for Health Statistics; 2025 Jun. doi:10.15620/cdc/174595. Table 3, weight in kilograms for adults age 20 and older, by sex. Read from the NCBI Bookshelf reproduction of Table 3.
notes: NHANES TABLE 3, ADULTS AGE 20 AND OLDER. Male mean 90.3 kg (SEM 0.9, n = 2,688); female mean 77.9 kg (SEM 0.8, n = 3,254). Sample sizes unweighted, estimates weighted to the US population. Pregnant females excluded. Pre-registered in validation/body_mass_prereg.md, committed at 3fd859b before the source was opened. pooling_rule = single-source, k = 1. THIS IS NOT THE SAME QUANTITY AS BF.BODY_MASS.REFERENCE AND MUST NOT BE MERGED WITH IT. The reference row is the mass at which this ledger's EXTENSIVE CONSTANTS are stated - GFR 180 L/day, cardiac output 7200 mL/min, blood volume 5.0 L are all textbook values for a roughly 70 kg, 1.73 m2 adult. It is a normalisation convention belonging to those sources, not a claim about how much people weigh. THIS row is a claim about how much people weigh. Setting the reference to 90.3 would scale GFR to 232 L/day by construction, which is not a measurement of anything - it would restate the same physiology against a different denominator and silently rescale every constant whose source assumed 70 kg. The prereg said the sexed pair 'must move the model'. It moves the POPULATION, which is where body mass actually lives; the single-individual default stays at the reference so that no existing result moves for a reason unrelated to this extraction. WHAT THIS EXPOSES, AND IT IS NOT SMALL: a typical US adult male at 90.3 kg is 1.29x the reference mass, and scaling.jl already records that linear-in-mass scaling OVERSTATES the spread of GFR and cardiac output, which are properly normalised to body surface area. Applying linear scaling out to 1.29x is using it at the edge of where it is defensible. The US adult population this describes has a mean BMI in the obese range, so the model's typical individual is now heavier than the lean reference adults in whom GFR0 and CO0 were characterised. That is a real limitation of using a population survey as a physiological reference and it is recorded rather than hidden.

name: Adult body mass, 5th percentile
citation: Fryar CD, Gu Q, Afful J, Carroll MD, Ogden CL. Anthropometric Reference Data for Children and Adults: United States, August 2021-August 2023. Vital and Health Statistics Series 3, No. 50. Atlanta (GA): National Center for Health Statistics; 2025 Jun. doi:10.15620/cdc/174595. Table 3, weight in kilograms for adults age 20 and older, by sex. Read from the NCBI Bookshelf reproduction of Table 3.
notes: NHANES Table 3 percentile, adults 20 and older, same source and extraction as BF.BODY_MASS.TYPICAL. Entered as a PERCENTILE, NOT converted to a standard deviation, and that is deliberate. The source reports a standard error of the MEAN and a percentile distribution; it does not report a population SD. Two standard estimators disagree materially because body weight is right-skewed - (P95-P05)/3.29 gives 21.6 kg for males while IQR/1.349 gives 18.7 kg, and the male mean 90.3 sits above the median 86.6 - so picking one AFTER seeing the numbers is exactly the unfalsifiable choice validation/pooling.md exists to prevent, and the pre-registration did not declare an SD estimator. NO SD IS ENTERED. The ensemble samples Sobol between these bounds, which is what sample_population actually does with its argument anyway - it only ever took the 1st and 99th percentiles of the distribution it was handed and sampled uniformly between them. KNOWN LIMITATION, now explicit rather than disguised by a Normal: the sampled population is UNIFORM over this range, not weight-distributed, so it over-represents the tails. Fixing that needs a declared distribution family and an SD estimator chosen in advance, which is its own pre-registration.

name: Fraction of total body sodium stored osmotically inactive
citation: Rakova N et al. Long-term space flight simulation reveals infradian rhythmicity in human Na+ balance. Cell Metab 2013;17(1):125-131.
notes: ASSUMED PLACEHOLDER. Rakova et al establish that total-body Na+ is stored and is NOT a simple function of salt intake, and that total-body Na+ and extracellular water are not tightly coupled. They do not report a single storage fraction. This value is a placeholder to make the third compartment functional and MUST be replaced by estimation against the Mars500 balance series. See ADR 0004. || OPENED THE SOURCES AND ENTERED NOTHING, AND THE REASON IS THAT NONE OF THEM MEASURES THIS QUANTITY. 2026-09-17, HANDOVER section 3.51. THREE DIFFERENT THINGS: this row is a STEADY-STATE RATIO, Na_store over Na_ecf. Olde Engberink 2017 (PMID 28132715, read in full) gives the fraction of cations ACUTELY CLEARED FROM BODY WATER that is not retrieved in urine over 4 h - 47 to 55 percent, a buffering fraction of a LOAD. Rakova 2013 (Cell Metab 17(1):125-131, Open Archive, read) gives the SWING AMPLITUDE of total-body sodium at fixed intake, plus or minus 200-400 mmol, without parallel changes in body weight or extracellular water. A buffering fraction, a swing amplitude and a steady-state ratio are not interchangeable, and entering any of them here is what section 3.1 of the pre-registration was written to prevent - it anticipated the 23Na MRI version of that trap and this is a different one. || AND SECTION 3.2's CAVEAT APPLIES AT FULL STRENGTH. Olde Engberink's quantity is INFERRED from a mismatch between plasma sodium change and urinary excretion through the Adrogue-Madias and Nguyen-Kurtz formulas; their own stated limitation is that they 'did not directly measure the amount of nonosmotic Na+ stored in the tissues'. Their subjects were SALT-DEPLETED, baseline fractional sodium excretion 0.08 percent, and the paper itself says the capacity may be large BECAUSE of that. || STAGE 1's DIAGNOSTIC OF ABOUT 0.40 IS NOT ENTERED AND MUST NOT BE. It is what the model needs to reproduce Drummer's half-life ratio, which is precisely what makes it inadmissible as a value. THE ROW STAYS ASSUMED.

name: Osmotically inactive sodium storage time constant
citation: Olde Engberink RHG, Rorije NMG, van den Born BJH, Vogt L. Quantification of nonosmotic sodium storage capacity following acute hypertonic saline infusion in healthy individuals. Kidney Int 2017;91(3):738-745. doi:10.1016/j.kint.2016.12.004. PMID 28132715. READ IN FULL. 12 healthy normotensive non-smoking men on a low-sodium diet, 2.4 percent NaCl over 30 min dosed to 5 mmol Na per L total body water, 4 h follow-up. Osmotic inactivation is measurable at 2 h and larger at 4 h: 92 +/- 26 mmol of sodium or potassium should have been excreted and 51 mmol was, so only 47 and 55 percent of expected sodium and potassium excretion were retrieved in urine.
notes: ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, NOT A MEASUREMENT, AND ONE SIGNIFICANT FIGURE FOR THAT REASON. 2026-09-17, HANDOVER section 3.52, validation/sodium_store_structure_prereg.md branch X1. A first-order store with tau = 0.1 d is 57 percent loaded at 2 h and 81 percent at 4 h, which is what Olde Engberink observes; the 0.05-0.2 d range is the span consistent with that observation window and nothing narrower is supportable. Directive 1.9. || WHAT IT REPLACES AND WHY THE OLD VALUE WAS WRONG IN KIND. The previous 7 d was taken from Rakova's circaseptan rhythm - and that paper reports 'peaks at about 6 DAYS period length', not 7. But the rounding was the small error: A RHYTHM PERIOD IS NOT A FIRST-ORDER RELAXATION TIME CONSTANT. An oscillation against a relaxation; no arithmetic converts one into the other. The row's own previous note admitted the value was 'chosen to match the reported weekly infradian rhythm period rather than derived from it'. Failure mode 11. || THE SCOPE DECISION THIS VALUE BELONGS TO. ADR 0004's single compartment is now explicitly scoped to the ACUTE process. Three timescales are in evidence - 2-4 h, about 6 days, monthly and longer - and one first-order compartment carries one. THE CIRCASEPTAN AND MONTHLY RHYTHMS ARE OUT OF SCOPE FOR THIS MODEL, declared rather than forgotten: it has no machinery to generate an infradian rhythm and no protocol longer than the 30-day salt step in which one would show. || IT OVERLAPS THE MODEL'S OWN REQUIREMENT AND THAT IS DECLARED. Stage 1's diagnostic wanted 0.05-0.25 d to reproduce Drummer's half-life ratio. This row is sourced from a DIFFERENT study, a different manoeuvre and a different tonicity, and 0.1 d is NOT the best-performing value in that sweep - 0.25 d was. Read the overlap as two independent routes agreeing that the process takes HOURS, which is the claim, and not as confirmation of either. || CAVEATS THAT STAY ON THE ROW. The source's quantity is INFERRED from a mismatch between plasma sodium change and urinary excretion through the Adrogue-Madias and Nguyen-Kurtz formulas, and its own limitation is that it 'did not directly measure the amount of nonosmotic Na+ stored in the tissues'. Subjects were SALT-DEPLETED - baseline fractional sodium excretion 0.08 percent - and the paper says the capacity may be large BECAUSE of that. HYPERTONIC, not isotonic. n = 12 men. Tier B and it does not improve. || NOTHING READS THIS ROW IN THE DEFAULT BUILD. storage defaults to false and ADR 0004 stays PROVISIONAL.

name: Relative amplitude of circadian modulation of renal sodium handling
citation: Kanabrocki EL, Scheving LE, Olwin JH, et al. Circadian variation in the urinary excretion of electrolytes and trace elements in men. Am J Anat 1983;166(2):121-148.
notes: STILL ASSUMED AT 0.25, AND NOW WITH THE CONFLICT RECORDED RATHER THAN A SINGLE SOURCE. A wide sweep of the circadian sodium literature found the amplitude genuinely contested. UPPER END: Kanabrocki 1983, 11 healthy adult males, 3-hourly urine over 27 h with cosinor analysis, found a statistically significant population rhythm for sodium and reported that for almost every element the increase from lowest to highest 3-hour group mean exceeded 100%. A peak-to-trough ratio of 2 corresponds to a cosinor amplitude of 0.33, and >100% is a lower bound, so this supports 0.33 or more. LOWER END: Peng 2021, 85 healthy Chinese adults, every voided specimen over 24 h with cosinor analysis, found URINARY SODIUM SHOWED NON-SIGNIFICANT PARAMETERS IN THE COSINOR MODEL and that the sodium rhythm was less significant than potassium. That is close to an amplitude of zero. 0.25 sits between them and is NOT a pooled estimate - pooling a significant and a non-significant result is not defensible. THE RHYTHM'S EXISTENCE IS BETTER SUPPORTED THAN ITS SIZE: see CIRC.RENAL_NA.ENDOGENEITY_MARKER. THE PROPER SOURCE HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED AND NOT YET OBTAINED - Minors and Waterhouse 1990 provide normative ENDOGENOUS urinary sodium data from about 80 constant routines, which is exactly the unmasked quantity this parameter should carry. Get it before trusting any circadian sodium result.

name: Time of peak renal sodium excretion
citation: Ueno M, Kawasaki T, Uezono K, Omae T, Matsuoka M. Relationship of urinary kallikrein excretion to renal water and sodium excretion. Metabolism 1983;32(5):433-437.
notes: STILL ASSUMED AT 0.33 day, AND THE ACROPHASE IS CONTESTED TOO - the two best cosinor studies found are nearly ANTIPHASE. Ueno 1983, 20 healthy Japanese women on an ordinary diet, cosinor: acrophase of urinary sodium excretion at 16:55, i.e. late afternoon, closely tracking urine volume at 16:51 (r = 0.935). Under this component's convention with a 07:00 active-period start that is 0.41 day. Peng 2021, 85 healthy Chinese adults, cosinor: sodium excretion had a NOCTURNAL PEAK falling to its lowest around noon to afternoon - roughly the opposite. 0.33 day (about 15:00) is retained as a placeholder consistent with Ueno and inconsistent with Peng. It is NOT a compromise between them; there is no defensible compromise between antiphase estimates. Resolve with the Minors and Waterhouse constant-routine normative data before this parameter is used for anything.

name: Endogenous circadian amplitude of mean arterial pressure, relative
citation: Shea SA, Hilton MF, Hu K, Scheer FAJL. Existence of an endogenous circadian blood pressure rhythm in humans that peaks in the evening. Circ Res 2011;108(8):980-984.

name: Lower limit of renal autoregulation
citation: Finke R, Gross R, Hackenthal E, Huber J, Kirchheim HR. Threshold pressure for the pressure-dependent renin release in the autoregulating kidney of conscious dogs. Pflugers Arch 1983;399(2):102-110. PMID 6139786. Lower limit of renal blood flow autoregulation, measured directly by servo-controlled stepwise reduction of renal artery pressure in the conscious animal.
notes: VALUE CHANGED 80.0 -> 63.9 mmHg ON 2026-08-27, AND SPECIES CORRECTED human -> dog. The previous value was NOT SOURCED: citation read 'Standard physiological reference. VERIFY.', which is not a reference, and species read 'human', which was not supported. This row was the last of the seven rows carrying that identical non-citation to be flagged as genuine debt rather than discharged, and HANDOVER 3.1 named it the one to look at first because CV.MAP.SETPOINT moved 93 -> 87 on the same day, carrying the operating point TOWARD this breakpoint. POOLING RULE, DECLARED BEFORE EXTRACTION per validation/pooling.md: single-source, n_studies k=1. No cross-species pooling was performed and no range midpoint was taken; both are prohibited for new entries. BRANCH 7 OF THE PRE-REGISTERED PROCEDURE WAS TAKEN. Branches 1-5 fail: NO human primary study reports a numeric lower breakpoint. The one that appears to - Textor SC et al, Ann Intern Med 1985;102(3):308-314, 'Critical perfusion pressure for renal function' - measures a STENOSIS threshold in bilateral atherosclerotic renovascular disease, not the intrinsic breakpoint of a normal kidney, and the sensitivity disappeared after revascularisation. Branch 6 fails too, and that is the finding of this pass: THE HUMAN EVIDENCE CONFLICTS AT THE SAME PRESSURE. At MAP 60 mmHg, Lessard MR and Trepanier CA, Anesthesiology 1991;74(5):860-865 (n=20, GFR by inulin, ERPF by PAH, MAP 59.8 +/- 0.4 for 237 min) found GFR not significantly further reduced and renal vascular resistance FALLING to maintain renal blood flow - the autoregulatory signature; while Hara T et al, J Clin Anesth 1998;10(7):539-545 (n=26, MAP 60 for 120 min) found creatinine clearance SIGNIFICANTLY DECREASED in both arms. Lessard is the methodologically stronger study, but choosing it after seeing both is precisely what pre-registration forbids, so branch 6's condition - that human studies ESTABLISH preservation - genuinely fails on its own terms. There is no lower pressure where the human evidence is unconflicted either: at MAP 50, Zayas VM et al, Am J Physiol 1993;265(5 Pt 2):F686-F692 and Toivonen J et al, Eur J Anaesthesiol 1991;8(1):13-20 both report renal function falling. ALL FOUR HUMAN STUDIES ARE ANAESTHESIA SAFETY STUDIES and directive 1.7 predicts what they returned: apply the test - had the physiology come out differently, the conclusion would have been 'this hypotensive technique is unsafe for the kidney'. The pressure-flow relationship is the INSTRUMENT there, not the subject, and every one of them carries a confound (volatile anaesthetic, sympathetic blockade, vasodilator, or all three), with anaesthesia depressing GFR before any pressure was lowered. THE ADOPTED SOURCE IS THE OPPOSITE KIND OF STUDY. name: Upper limit of renal autoregulation
citation: Roman RJ, Cowley AW Jr. Characterization of a new model for the study of pressure-natriuresis in the rat. Am J Physiol 1985;248:F190-F198. PMID 3970209. Highest renal perfusion pressure at which GFR was measured and found unchanged.
notes: EVIDENCE UNDER AN ETHICAL CEILING, NOT DEBT (ADR 0006 amended 2026-08-21). The rat provenance of this value is not a deficiency to be burned down. No human study raises arterial pressure to locate the failure of GFR autoregulation and none may; the human literature only ever lowers it. Where the human experiment cannot ethically exist, a well-conducted animal study is the evidence, not a substitute for it. This row is E2 with species, preparation and tested range recorded. WHAT REMAINS A REAL LIMITATION IS THE CENSORING, NOT THE SPECIES: 160 mmHg was the highest RPP tested in that preparation, so the true breakpoint is >= 160 and is not known to BE 160. UPPER BREAKPOINT MOVED 180 -> 160 mmHg ON 2026-08-21. The previous value was NOT SOURCED: citation read 'Standard physiological reference. VERIFY.' and species read 'human', neither of which was true. POOLING RULE, DECLARED BEFORE EXTRACTION per validation/pooling.md, pre-registration in validation/autoreg_upper_prereg.md: single-source, n_studies k=1. The pre-registration fixed, before any paper was read, that if zero HUMAN primary studies reported an upper breakpoint then the value could not be retained by cross-species pooling or by range-midpoint (both prohibited) and had to be brought inside the range where the model's own relations have support. SEARCH RESULT - THERE IS NO HUMAN PRIMARY EVIDENCE FOR AN UPPER BREAKPOINT. PubMed yields no human study that RAISES arterial pressure and measures the pressure at which GFR autoregulation fails; for obvious reasons the human literature only ever probes the LOWER limb by LOWERING pressure - Parving HH et al, Diabetologia 1984;27:547-552 (clonidine, MAP fall 16-18 mmHg, PMID 6442240), New JP et al, Diabetologia 1998;41:206-211 (trandolapril, MAP 103->93, PMID 9498655), Christensen PK et al, Kidney Int 2001 (PMID 11576357) and Diabetes Care 2003 (PMID 12502673). None of these reaches 160 mmHg, let alone 180. WHERE 180 ACTUALLY CAME FROM: Shipley RE, Study RS, Am J Physiol 1951;167:676-688, doi 10.1152/ajplegacy.1951.167.3.676, PMID 14903093 - DOG, acute alterations of renal artery pressure. That is the primary origin of the textbook '80-180 mmHg' and it is canine. (The PubMed MeSH record for PMID 14903093 carries the term 'Humans'; that is a known legacy-indexing artefact of the AJP back-catalogue, contradicted by the paper and by every secondary source that cites it as the canine range. Recorded here because the MeSH tag would otherwise look like human support.) 180 therefore entered this ledger as a dog number wearing a human label. WHAT IS ADOPTED: Roman RJ, Cowley AW Jr, Am J Physiol 1985;248:F190-F198, doi 10.1152/ajprenal.1985.248.2.F190, PMID 3970209. RAT, denervated kidney, vasopressin, aldosterone, corticosterone and noradrenaline clamped by infusion, RPP set by aortic clamp. Verbatim: 'Increasing RPP within the autoregulatory range from 90 to 160 mmHg produced 5- to 20-fold increases in urine flow and sodium excretion with no detectable changes in glomerular filtration rate, renal blood flow, or peritubular capillary pressure.' That is a direct primary measurement that GFR autoregulation is INTACT at 160 mmHg. THIS IS A CENSORED OBSERVATION, NOT A MEASURED BREAKPOINT. 160 mmHg is the highest RPP Roman and Cowley tested, so the true upper limit is >= 160; it is not known to BE 160. uncertainty_type is 'none' rather than a range because inventing a 160-180 interval would smuggle back the range-midpoint reasoning pooling.md prohibits. The model breakpoint is set at the edge of evidence, which is the conservative direction: it makes GFR fall with pressure slightly earlier than reality, rather than asserting a flat plateau in a region nothing has measured. WHY 160 AND NOT SOMETHING ELSE - THE TWO CONSTRAINTS COINCIDE. Roman and Cowley 1985 is ALSO the form source for the model's pressure natriuresis (see RN.PRESSURE_NATRIURESIS.SLOPE and ledger/relations.csv row Renal.FR_effective), where the LINEAR form is evidenced over roughly 55-160 mmHg. At 180 the autoregulation breakpoint sat OUTSIDE the range over which the equation it modifies has any support, so the model contained a kink in a region where its own natriuresis term was unevidenced. Setting the breakpoint to 160 makes the autoregulatory plateau and the natriuresis validity range terminate together, at the same pressure, from the SAME primary paper. That is not a coincidence chosen after the fact - the <=160 ceiling was written into the pre-registration before extraction. CROSS-SPECIES POOLING NOT PERFORMED, as prohibited. The dog value (Shipley 1951) and the rat value (Roman 1985) are NOT averaged. One rat study is adopted; the dog study is recorded as provenance archaeology for the discarded 180, not as a co-estimate. CORROBORATION, RECORDED AS CONTEXT AND NOT POOLED: Cupples WA, Braam B, Am J Physiol Renal Physiol 2007;292:F1105-F1123, doi 10.1152/ajprenal.00194.2006, describe the plateau as spanning from ~75 mmHg (dogs) or ~85 mmHg (rats) to >160 mmHg - note '>160', an open upper bound, not a fixed 180. Carlstrom M, Wilcox CS, Arendshorst WJ, Physiol Rev 2015;95:405-511, doi 10.1152/physrev.00042.2012, quote the conventional 80-180 mmHg. Both are reviews (tier B) and neither adds human primary data on the upper limit. SPECIES CHANGED human -> rat. TIER CHANGED B -> A: per SOURCES.md, tier A includes 'peer-reviewed primary research in animal models, flagged as such with species noted'. The tier RISES because the source is now a primary measurement rather than an unnamed reference, while the species flag FALLS to rat. Those are two separate axes and both moved honestly. KNOWN LIMITATION: the model is human. A rat autoregulatory breakpoint is being used in a human model because no human number exists. This is species extrapolation and is flagged as such. NO NUMERICAL EFFECT AT THE OPERATING POINT: IPE runs at MAP ~88-93 mmHg, inside [80, 160], where GFR ~ GFR0 either way. Verified: the ADR 0007 salt-step result is unchanged. The change buys honesty and removes an unevidenced kink, not different behaviour. WHAT IS STILL NOT SOURCED: the piecewise-flat-then-proportional FORM of the autoregulation equation, including its derivative discontinuity at both breakpoints. Only the breakpoint VALUE is sourced here. ledger/relations.csv row Renal.GFR therefore remains in the grandfathered unsourced list in tools/check_relations.py and its form_citation stays empty. LEDGER SCHEMA DEBT: validation/pooling.md specifies pooling_rule, n_studies and pooling_notes as columns of this CSV. Those columns do not exist yet, so the rule is recorded in prose here, following the precedent already set by RN.PRESSURE_NATRIURESIS.SLOPE. SCALING FROM RAT TO HUMAN: NO SCALING FACTOR IS APPLIED, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE CLAIM, NOT AN OMISSION. This parameter is a PRESSURE (mmHg), an intensive variable, unlike the extensive quantities in this ledger (GFR, sodium excretion, blood volume) which would require allometric scaling by body or kidney mass. Mean arterial pressure in the conscious rat (~100-120 mmHg) and in the adult human (~93 mmHg here) are the same order of magnitude, and the autoregulatory plateau is generated by afferent-arteriolar myogenic tone and tubuloglomerular feedback, which are transmural-pressure-sensing mechanisms operating on the same pressure scale in both species rather than mass-dependent ones. name: Hematocrit
citation: Morales-Mendoza E, Suarez-Ramos MDP, Godoy-Corredor M, Gomez-Lopera N, Combariza-Vallejo JF, Murcia J, Isaza-Ruget MA. Reference intervals for hemoglobin and hematocrit adjusted for altitude, sex, and age: a big data-based study in the Colombian population. Med Sci (Basel) 2026;14(1):136. doi:10.3390/medsci14010136. PMID 41892851. 662,024 hematocrit results from apparently healthy adults, 2022-2024, stratified by sex, age and residential altitude; LOW-ALTITUDE stratum (<1100 m a.s.l.) taken.
notes: CHANGED 0.45 `both` -> 0.453 male / 0.395 female ON 2026-08-28. The previous value was NOT SOURCED: citation read 'Standard physiological reference. VERIFY.' while extraction_method claimed `reported`. Pre-registered in validation/verify_rows_prereg.md at e0195f4. pooling_rule = single-source, k = 1. THE INCUMBENT 0.45 WAS ESSENTIALLY THE MALE VALUE APPLIED TO EVERYONE. That is the specific shape of the error here, and it is why the prereg fixed in advance that this row was expected to be dimorphic: androgen-driven erythropoiesis is not a body-size effect and does not dissolve into body_mass. THE VALUE: median hematocrit in the LOW-ALTITUDE stratum, men 18-64 45.3% and women 18-50 39.5%. The low-altitude stratum is taken deliberately - hematocrit rises with residential altitude, and this model carries no altitude. In the same cohort the men's median climbs 45.3 -> 48.9% from <1100 m to 2000-3000 m, so choosing the stratum matters more than the choice between plausible sources. Medians rather than means because the paper reports medians. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION, DELIBERATELY NOT POOLED: Fulgoni VL 3rd, Agarwal S, Kellogg MD, Lieberman HR. Establishing pediatric and adult RBC reference intervals with NHANES data using piecewise regression. Am J Clin Pathol 2019;151(2):128-142. PMID 30285066. NHANES 1999-2012, n = 44,328, nationally representative US healthy population. It reports REFERENCE INTERVALS, not central values: male 20-35 y 40.2-51.0%, female 20-45 y 32.5-45.2%. Both adopted medians sit comfortably inside those intervals. It is NOT pooled with the Colombian medians - an interval and a median are not the same statistic, the populations differ, and pooling.md prohibits range-midpoint for new entries, which is the only way an interval could have been turned into a point estimate here. FULGONI INDEPENDENTLY MAKES THE TEXTBOOK POINT: it reports that suggested hematocrit and haemoglobin reference values for older adult males are SUBSTANTIALLY LOWER than current standards - a male lower limit of 35.0% at 71-79 years against a non-age-based conventional 38.8%. THE MODEL IS CURRENTLY INSENSITIVE TO THIS ROW, AND THAT IS A STRUCTURAL FACT WORTH KNOWING RATHER THAN A REASON NOT TO SOURCE IT. Haematocrit enters only through V_blood = f_pv*V_ecf/(1-Hct), and CV.PLASMA.ECF_FRACTION is DERIVED as BV0*(1-Hct)/V_ecf, so f_pv/(1-Hct) = BV0/V_ecf identically and the haematocrit cancels. Verified empirically: entering this pair left every simulated result bit-identical. It will bite the moment f_pv is sourced independently - plasma volume as a fraction of extracellular volume is directly measurable - or when anything depending on viscosity or oxygen carriage exists. Until then this row is honest provenance for a quantity the model reports but does not yet use. || THIS ROW BECAME IDENTIFIABLE ON 2026-09-02, AND HANDOVER SECTION 3.5 SAID IT WOULD NOT. That section recorded haematocrit as non-identifiable: CV.PLASMA.ECF_FRACTION is DERIVED as BV0*(1-Hct)/V_ecf, so f_pv/(1-Hct) = BV0/V_ecf and this row cancelled out of every result - verified empirically at the time, a 15% sex difference leaving every output identical to seven figures. THAT CANCELLATION IS IN THE LEVEL ONLY. Cardiovascular.jl computed V_blood as V_plasma/(1-Hct) with Hct constant, which makes red cell volume expand with plasma; over a 30 day salt step red cell mass is fixed, so that was wrong. The equation is now V_blood ~ V_plasma + Hct*BV0, and the DERIVATIVE dV_blood/dV_ecf is f_pv = BV0*(1-Hct)/V_ecf0, which depends on this row. The sourced 0.453/0.395 pair now moves a result: the male/female ECF excursion ratio goes 1.069 -> 1.182, and the part that is new is entirely haematocrit because it is the only term that stopped cancelling. ADR 0014's falsifiable test is satisfied a second time. THE GENERAL LESSON, RECORDED BECAUSE IT COST TWO WRONG CONCLUSIONS: a parameter can be non-identifiable in a model's steady-state LEVELS and identifiable in its RESPONSES, so testing whether a pair moves the answer at one operating point is not a test of identifiability at all.

name: Cardiac output sensitivity to blood volume
citation: Diaz-Canestro C, Pentz B, Sehgal A, Montero D. Blood withdrawal acutely impairs cardiac filling, output and aerobic capacity in proportion to induced hypovolemia in middle-aged and older women. Appl Physiol Nutr Metab 2022;47(1):75-82. doi:10.1139/apnm-2021-0196. PMID 34875180. n = 30 healthy women. Supporting: Fortney 1983 PMID 6629925 (both limbs, n=5 healthy men); Bundgaard-Nielsen 2010 PMID 20545713 (n=20 healthy supine); Nguyen 1988 PMID 2901018 (n=8 healthy men); Kanstrup 1982 PMID 7096143.
notes: SOURCED IN HEALTHY HUMANS 2026-09-03, 2880 -> 1400, `calibrated` -> `derived`. Pre-registered in validation/venous_return_human_prereg.md; reproduce with python validation/venous_return_human_extract.py. HANDOVER section 4 item 2 and section 7. || THE EARLIER SEARCH MISSED IT BY LOOKING FOR THE WRONG OBJECT. This row is dCO/dV_blood, NOT a compliance in mL/mmHg. Section 3.9 records a whole line of work withdrawn for composing a compliance and a resistance into it while treating right atrial pressure as fixed. Blood volume can be changed by a KNOWN amount in healthy people - withdrawal, or plasma expansion - and cardiac output measured, so the composite is directly measurable in a performable paradigm. || THE VALUE, from the resting withdrawal limb. Diaz-Canestro C, Pentz B, Sehgal A, Montero D. Appl Physiol Nutr Metab 2022;47(1):75-82, PMID 34875180: 30 healthy women aged 47-77, non-smokers, non-obese, blood volume 3.8-6.6 L; a standard 10% reduction of blood volume (0.5 +/- 0.1 L withdrawn, haematocrit unchanged) reduced left ventricular end-diastolic volume and stroke volume by at least 10% AT REST, P <= 0.009. On a female cardiac output of 4.88 L/min that is 0.98 (L/min)/L = 1404 (L/day)/L, entered as 1400. The paper's title is 'in proportion to induced hypovolemia' - the relationship IS the subject, directive 1.7. || IT IS AN UPPER BOUND AND IS ENTERED AS ONE. A study reporting STROKE volume bounds dCO/dV from above, because heart rate can compensate; the pre-registration said so before the search. Three expansion studies all indicate the true resting value is at or below it and none resolves how far: Bundgaard-Nielsen 2010 (PMID 20545713, n=20 healthy supine) gave 200 mL of colloid and NO subject raised stroke volume by 10%, with cardiac output and heart rate both unchanged; Nguyen 1988 (PMID 2901018, n=8 healthy men) expanded intravascular volume 10-11% with hypertonic saline for small NON-SIGNIFICANT changes in stroke volume and cardiac index; Kanstrup 1982 (PMID 7096143) found cardiac output rose after 700 mL but reports no resting magnitude. || ASYMMETRY, MEASURED, AND IT NEARLY FAILED THE PRE-REGISTERED TEST. Fortney SM, Wenger CB, Bove JR, Nadel ER. J Appl Physiol 1983;55(3):884-90, PMID 6629925 is the only study giving BOTH limbs in the SAME 5 healthy men under the same protocol: -490 mL gave -2.2 L/min and +440 mL gave +1.0 L/min, i.e. 4.49 against 2.27 (L/min)/L, a ratio of 1.98 against a failure threshold of 2 fixed before the numbers. It passes by 1 percent. A LINEAR SYMMETRIC GAIN IS AT THE EDGE OF WHAT THIS EVIDENCE SUPPORTS, and the direction is the expected one - the heart sits nearer the flat part of its filling curve above normovolemia than below. Those figures are at 65-70 percent of VO2max and are recorded as evidence about the FORM; the pre-registration fixed that resting values govern, because the salt step is a resting protocol. || TWO INDEPENDENT LINES AGREE AND THAT IS THE RESULT. Chronic sodium balance implies 1012-1941 (HANDOVER 3.7, 3.8) from human pressure and volume responses. Acute volume manipulation in healthy people gives 1400. The two share no data, no subjects, no measurement and no timescale. THE MODEL WAS 2.06x TOO STIFF, which is inside the 1.5-2.1x that section 3.7 estimated from the salt data alone. || NOT CIRCULAR, AND CHECKABLE. The pre-registration forbade choosing a value to land the salt step in the human window, because the salt data are the TEST and may not also be the estimator. 1400 does NOT land it in the window; a value chosen to pass would have been nearer 1700. || STILL UNSOURCED IN HEALTHY HUMANS: systemic venous compliance in mL/mmHg, mean systemic filling pressure, and resistance to venous return. The one human compliance value found is Takatsu 1989 (PMID 2545936), 2.3 +/- 0.7 mL/mmHg/kg - close to the anaesthetised dog and pig values already held - but its cohort is 56 CARDIAC PATIENTS graded by NYHA class and even class I is cardiac patients. The pre-registration excluded NYHA class I in advance. Those three quantities are no longer NEEDED, because the composite was sourced directly. || PREVIOUS NOTE PRESERVED: CALIBRATED, not measured. Originating model: Guyton 1972. The Frank-Starling and venous return relationships are E1; this linearised sensitivity around the operating point is a fitted constant. Second most consequential unmeasured number after the pressure natriuresis slope - together these two set the loop gain. || THE TEST THAT SHOULD SET THIS ROW HAS NOW BEEN RUN, AND IT GIVES A NUMBER: 2880 SHOULD BE ABOUT 554. 2026-09-02, from ADR 0013's falsifiable test - validation/ecf_salt_response_extract.py. This row sets dMAP/dV_ecf, which is 11.285 mmHg/L at the 70 kg reference and scales as 1/mass. van den Bosch 2021 (n = 70 healthy men, ECFV by iothalamate and blood pressure in the SAME subjects, intake verified by 24 h urinary sodium) gives 1.885 mmHg/L at 80.6 kg, which is 2.170 at the 70 kg reference and corresponds to G_vr = 554. THE MODEL IS 5.2x TOO STIFF ON PRESSURE PER UNIT VOLUME. This is measurable independently of G_pn: an 8x change in this row moves the salt-step PRESSURE response by 0.12% while moving the VOLUME response exactly inversely, so the two parameters are orthogonal and each is identified by its own human datum. DO NOT SIMPLY REFIT IT TO 554. This row is `calibrated` and HANDOVER section 4 item 1 is to REPLACE it with sourced venous compliance - Pmsf, right atrial pressure, stressed versus unstressed volume. 554 is the target that work now has to explain, not a value to enter; entering it would swap one fitted constant for another and lose the falsifiable test in the process. name: Sympathetic arterial baroreflex open-loop gain
citation: Yamasaki F, Sato T, Sato K, Diedrich A. Analytic and integrative framework for understanding human sympathetic arterial baroreflex function. Front Neurosci 2021;15:707345.
notes: 2.0 -> 5.62 ON 2026-09-09, AT THE OWNER'S EXPLICIT INSTRUCTION, AND THE CITATION DID NOT CHANGE. The note also repeated his sentence that the invasive approach is not applicable to humans and that human open-loop gain HAS NOT BEEN CLARIFIED. || THAT SENTENCE IS THE PAPER'S PROBLEM STATEMENT AND THE PAPER IS THE ANSWER TO IT. Yamasaki F, Sato T, Sato K, Diedrich A. Front Neurosci 2021;15:707345, PMC8322947, OPEN ACCESS, READ IN FULL. He measured it in humans: GL(0) = 5.62 +/- 0.98 SUPINE and GL(15) = 3.75 +/- 0.62 at 15 degrees head-up tilt. Table 2, and both Methods and the table legend state 'Values are means +/- SD'. citation: Saturation bound; see notes.

citation: Derived from BR.CARDIAC.SENSITIVITY, CV.HR.NOMINAL and CV.MAP.SETPOINT.
notes: DERIVED 2026-09-08, and it is what Baroreflex.jl actually reads. BR.CARDIAC.GAIN = BR.CARDIAC.SENSITIVITY * CV.HR.NOMINAL * CV.MAP.SETPOINT / 60000. Male: 15.0 * 62.0 * 87.0 / 60000 = 1.34850. Female: 10.2 * 65.0 * 87.0 / 60000 = 0.961350. Asserted in tools/check_closure.py. || THE ARITHMETIC, AND IT WAS FIXED IN THE PRE-REGISTRATION BEFORE ANY VALUE WAS KNOWN. With RR = 60000/HR in ms, a sensitivity BRS = dRR/dP gives (1/HR)(dHR/dP) = -(HR/60000)*BRS, and multiplying by MAP_ref makes it the dimensionless gain this component's tanh consumes, matching the form BR.OPEN_LOOP_GAIN already sits in. || EVERY DIGIT IS CARRIED BECAUSE THIS ROW CLOSES AN IDENTITY, which is the lesson CV.CO.NOMINAL recorded when it held this position. The values are exact decimals, not rounded ones. The INPUT significant figures are three, and no result computed from this row may be quoted to more - directive 1.9. || THE CONVERSION IS LOCAL AND THAT IS A SCALE STATEMENT, NOT A CAVEAT. The relation between rate and interval is a reciprocal, so this factor holds at the operating heart rate and nowhere else. pooling.md requires two rows to share a measurement SCALE and not merely a unit symbol - section 5 item 18, the free-thyroxine error - and this is the line where that is honoured. A sensitivity measured at one heart rate cannot be composed with a different operating rate without redoing this conversion. || IT IS SEXED TWICE OVER AND THE TWO DIMORPHISMS ARE INDEPENDENT FACTS. The sensitivity is a male/female pair, and CV.HR.NOMINAL is a second one, 62 against 65. Neither is evidence for the other and the product carries both. This row would be sexed even if the sensitivity were entered as `both`. || WHAT IT IS AGAINST. Section 7.1 of the pre-registration predicted 'the same order' from the conversion factor alone, before any source was opened, and that is why section 6 was made the stop condition rather than a caveat. || AND IT DOES NOT DOUBLE-COUNT BR.OPEN_LOOP_GAIN - see that row, which now records why. name: Maximum fractional change in heart rate from baroreflex
citation: Saturation bound; see notes.
notes: ASSUMED, and it is the same convention BR.TPR.MAX_FRACTION carries for the vasomotor arm - 0.5, entered for the same reason and with the same standing, which is none. name: Vagal chronotropic effector time constant
citation: La Rovere MT, Pinna GD, Raczak G. Baroreflex sensitivity: measurement and clinical implications. Ann Noninvasive Electrocardiol 2008;13(2):191-207.
notes: ADDED 2026-09-08 BECAUSE THE MODEL DEMANDED IT, NOT BECAUSE THE PRE-REGISTRATION WANTED IT. validation/chronotropic_baroreflex_prereg.md section 5 made the chronotropic arm ALGEBRAIC by default and put the burden on ADDING a lag, on the directive 1.10 grounds that a 200-600 ms effector is quasi-static against a six-hour protocol. THAT WAS REFUTED BY BUILDING IT. || WHY. An algebraic hr_mod closes an INSTANTANEOUS ALGEBRAIC LOOP through arterial pressure: cardiac output sets MAP, MAP sets the baroreflex error, the error sets heart rate, and heart rate sets cardiac output. structural_simplify resolved it by promoting Blood.CO to a state - so the 'stateless' arm cost a state anyway, in another component, where it meant nothing. The vasomotor arm never had this problem because BR.EFFECTOR.TAU makes tpr_mod a STATE, and a lag is exactly what breaks an algebraic loop. || SO THE STATE IS PAID FOR EITHER WAY AND THIS IS THE HONEST PLACE TO PUT IT: on a variable with a physical meaning and a sourced time constant, rather than on an implicit nonlinear unknown inside the blood component. Ten states before, eleven after, and the eleventh is br.hr_mod. || THE VALUE. La Rovere reports the parasympathetic limb of the baroreflex acting on heart rate in 200-600 ms, against 2-3 s for the sympathetic vasomotor limb - the same sentence BR.EFFECTOR.TAU is entered from, and the reason ADR 0009 gave for lumping the arms in the first place. 0.4 s is the midpoint of that reported range, entered the same way BR.EFFECTOR.TAU takes 3.0 from 2.0-3.0. THE RANGE IS THE UNCERTAINTY AND IT IS THREEFOLD. || IT IS SEVEN TIMES FASTER THAN THE VASOMOTOR EFFECTOR, which is the physiology: vagal transmission is fast and cholinergic, sympathetic vasomotor transmission is slow and noradrenergic. That ratio is now the smallest declared time constant in the model and it widens the stiffness range - 0.4 s against a 10.3 day thyroxine turnover is about 2.2 million. ADR 0003 stays deferred on state count, but this is the fastest thing in the model and a multirate partition may not cut across it. || IT IS ALSO WHAT THE COUPLING DECLARATION READS. baroreflex_couplings() carried a hardcoded 0.5 s for one commit, which is directive 1.4's violation - a number in a component rather than in the ledger. It now reads this row.

name: Renal perfusion pressure above which renin release plateaus
citation: van Ochten M, El Fathi W, Bovee EME, Spaanderman MEA, Hooijmans CR, van Drongelen J. The renal baroreflex: a systematic review and meta-analysis in healthy and hypertensive animals. Physiol Rep 2025;13(17):e70547.
notes: THE COINCIDENCE IS BROKEN AS OF 2026-08-27, AND IT WAS THE FRAGILITY THIS ROW WARNED ABOUT. This threshold, 93 mmHg from van Ochten, used to equal CV.MAP.SETPOINT exactly, so the model sat ON the rectification point and RAAS was inactive at baseline BY CONSTRUCTION. The note said that rested on one unverified number. It did: the setpoint was the textbook brachial 120/80 convention and is now 87.0, derived from sourced central pressure. The model therefore sits 6 mmHg BELOW threshold and RAAS IS NOW ACTIVE AT REST - renin drive 0.069, plasma renin activity 2.31x baseline. That is more physiological, not less: resting renin is not zero. || Meta-analysis of 30 animal studies: renin falls linearly with rising renal pressure and plateaus above 93 +/- 2 mmHg. ADR 0006 E2 - servo-controlling renal perfusion pressure is not performable in humans, the same ethical ceiling as RN.PRESSURE_NATRIURESIS.SLOPE. QUALITY CAVEAT FROM THE PAPER ITSELF: risk of bias was high in most studies. FRAGILITY, RECORDED: this threshold equals CV.MAP.SETPOINT = 93.0, whose own citation reads 'Standard physiological reference. VERIFY.' The model therefore sits exactly ON the rectification threshold and RAAS is inactive at and above baseline BY CONSTRUCTION. That coincidence is doing structural work and rests on one unverified number. Verified against PubMed record PMID 40930784 on 2026-08-25. SCALING: none applied, and none is needed. The quantity is a PRESSURE THRESHOLD in mmHg, and arterial pressure is not body-size scaled across the mammals in this meta-analysis the way a flow or a volume would be - the threshold is reported in the same units the model uses. What is assumed instead is that the threshold TRANSFERS to humans unchanged, which is a species assumption rather than a scaling one, and it is the assumption to attack if this component misbehaves. Note the meta-analysis itself found the threshold comparable between healthy and hypertensive animals while the slope differed, which is weak evidence that the threshold is the more transferable of the two. || ROUNDED 2026-09-09 TO MEASUREMENT PRECISION at the owner's instruction. Nothing physiological in this model is measured to more than four significant figures, and trailing zeros on a whole number read as precision that is not there. The discarded digits were floating-point residue from the derivation, not information. Directive 1.13.

name: Rightward shift of the renin pressure threshold at saturating renal sympathetic activity
citation: Kirchheim HR, Finke R, Hackenthal E, Lowe W, Persson P. Baroreflex sympathetic activation increases threshold pressure for the pressure-dependent renin release in conscious dogs. Pflugers Arch 1985;405(2):127-135.
notes: SOURCED 2026-09-18 FROM KIRCHHEIM 1985, renal_sympathetic_prereg.md amendment 1. SEVEN chronically instrumented CONSCIOUS FOXHOUNDS, daily sodium 6.1 mmol/kg, renal artery pressure reduced in steps with an inflatable cuff and a pressure control system and held 5 min at each step. Stimulus-response curves of the renal-venous-arterial plasma renin activity difference against mean renal artery pressure. ABSTRACT ONLY - Pflugers Arch 1985 is paywalled and no PMC record exists; the abstract carries the numbers with dispersion, which is why the row is possible at all. Directive 1.5: the MEDLINE abstract was opened, the full text was not. || THE EFFECT IS A THRESHOLD SHIFT AND NOT A GAIN CHANGE, WHICH IS WHY THIS ROW EXISTS RATHER THAN A SYMPATHETIC RENIN GAIN. Common carotid occlusion shifted the stimulus-response curve to the RIGHT: threshold pressure 92.7 +/- 2.8 -> 109.7 +/- 4.1 mmHg (P < 0.05), while the PLATEAU level was unchanged (0.98 +/- 0.14 vs 0.99 +/- 0.14 ng AI/ml/h) and the SLOPE below threshold was unchanged (-0.379 +/- 0.041 vs -0.416 +/- 0.082 ng AI/ml/h/mmHg). The pre-registration assumed a gain and was wrong; opening the source is what caught it. || 109.7 - 92.7 = 17.0 mmHg, TWO SIGNIFICANT FIGURES. The SEs combine to about 5 mmHg, so the shift is 17 +/- 5 and the range on this row is one pooled SE either way. n = 7 dogs. Directive 1.13: nothing derived from this may carry three figures. || IT IS THE SHIFT AT NEAR-MAXIMAL CAROTID ACTIVATION, NOT A SLOPE. Carotid occlusion removes sinus baroreceptor input; Gross 1981 in the same laboratory reports bilateral occlusion raising systemic pressure 51 +/- 6.3 mmHg, so the stimulus is large. The model therefore applies this as the shift at SATURATING renal sympathetic activity and interpolates with the tanh the baroreflex already uses for its vasomotor efferent. THAT INTERPOLATION IS AN ASSUMPTION AND NOT KIRCHHEIM'S: he measured two points, control and occlusion, and no submaximal curve. || AND THE THRESHOLD IT SHIFTS WAS INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED BY THE SAME PAPER. RAAS.RENIN.PRESSURE_THRESHOLD is 93 +/- 2 mmHg from van Ochten's 2025 meta-analysis of 30 mostly-rodent studies whose own limitations say risk of bias was high in most; Kirchheim's conscious dogs give 92.7 +/- 2.8 by a different method in a different species. Nobody arranged that agreement. || MECHANISM CONTROL, Gross R et al. J Physiol 1981;313:237-250, PMID 7024507, twelve conscious foxhounds: with renal perfusion pressure held at control, carotid occlusion changed renin release in NEITHER the surgically denervated kidney (n = 3) NOR the intact kidney after beta-adrenergic blockade (n = 4), and renal blood flow did not change. So the pathway is DIRECT BETA-ADRENERGIC on the juxtaglomerular cells, with no vasomotor component - which is why this row moves a renin threshold and touches no haemodynamic quantity. || SPECIES: DOG, conscious, chronically instrumented. Directive 1.15 - the owner's standing default for neurogenic control of pressure through renal or baroreceptor mechanisms where no usable human measurement exists, and servo-control of renal artery pressure is not performable in humans, the same ethical ceiling that applies to RN.PRESSURE_NATRIURESIS.SLOPE and to the threshold this row shifts. || SETTING THIS ROW TO 0 RECOVERS THE PREVIOUS MODEL EXACTLY, on the precedent RN.MD.RENIN_GAIN was introduced on. No new structural variant and no new compilation. || SCALING: NONE, AND THAT IS AN ARGUMENT RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. This row is a difference of two ARTERIAL PRESSURES, which is an INTENSIVE quantity - it carries no mass or surface-area dimension, so the body-size scaling that BF.SIZE.EXPONENT applies to extensive rows does not apply here and multiplying by a mass ratio would be wrong. Dog and human operate at similar arterial pressures: Kirchheim's conscious foxhounds sit at a control threshold of 92.7 mmHg and Lohmeier's conscious dogs at a control MAP of 92 +/- 4 and 98 +/- 4 mmHg, against this model's central MAP setpoint of 87 mmHg and a renin threshold of 93. The pressures the two species regulate are the same to within the dispersion of either, so the shift transfers directly. WHAT DOES NOT TRANSFER WITHOUT ASSUMPTION is the mapping from carotid occlusion to this model's normalised sympathetic activity, which is stated above and is the real cross-species risk on this row - not the units.

Modelling that as first-order recovery reaching 95% at 5 days gives tau = 5/ln(20) = 1.669 day. name: Fractional renin rise per fractional fall in perfusion pressure
citation: van Ochten M, El Fathi W, Bovee EME, Spaanderman MEA, Hooijmans CR, van Drongelen J. The renal baroreflex: A systematic review and meta-analysis in healthy and hypertensive animals. Physiol Rep 2025;13(17):e70547. doi:10.14814/phy2.70547. PMID 40930784. PMC12422813. THE SLOPE, section 3.3.2 and Figure 6, read as full text: 'A decrease of 10 mmHg in renal blood pressure leads to an increase of 50 percentage points renin in healthy animals', where renin is expressed as a percentage of the value at the baseline mean renal arterial pressure of 110 mmHg, set to 100%. That baseline is ABOVE the 93 mmHg threshold, so the 100% reference IS the plateau - which is exactly what pra = 1 means in Raas.jl. Slope = 0.05 of plateau renin per mmHg.
notes: RE-DERIVED 2026-09-02, 19.0 -> 4.35, AND THE ROW STOPS BEING `assumed`. Pre-registered in validation/renin_gain_prereg.md, written before any source was opened and sitting before this change in history; verify with git log --diff-filter=A on that file. Reproduce with python validation/renin_gain_extract.py. Branch R1. || THE DERIVATION, and it is one line. Raas.jl sets pra -> 1 + g_renin*(P_thr - MAP)/MAP_ref, so d(pra)/d(MAP) = -g_renin/MAP_ref, and pra is normalised to the plateau. van Ochten reports the same derivative as 0.05 of plateau renin per mmHg. Therefore g_renin = 0.05 * MAP_ref = 0.05 * 87.0 = 4.35. || THE PREVIOUS NOTE ON THIS ROW WAS WRONG ABOUT THE SOURCE, AND THAT IS WHY THE ROW SAT `assumed` FOR SIX DAYS. It said van Ochten 'reports the renal baroreflex slope in animal units this model cannot consume directly, so the gain is fitted rather than converted.' The paper says the opposite in its own Limitations: it could NOT meta-analyse absolute renin because studies reported PRA, PRC or renin release on assay-dependent scales, so it converted the dose-response to PERCENTAGE OF BASELINE - which is the one form this model can consume, because pra here is dimensionless and normalised. The units were never the obstacle. Nobody had opened the paper. || ONE SIGNIFICANT FIGURE IN THE SOURCE, THREE IN THE VALUE, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS ARITHMETIC NOT PRECISION. '50 percentage points per 10 mmHg' carries one figure. 4.35 is stored so that g_renin = 0.05*MAP_ref reproduces exactly and stays exact if CV.MAP.SETPOINT moves again; the third digit is the conversion, not a measurement. Directive 1.9. A test asserts the identity rather than the digits. || SPECIES AND TIER. Animal, mixed (rat, dog, mouse, rabbit, cat, fowl). ADR 0006 E2 under an ethical ceiling: servo-controlling renal perfusion pressure is not performable in humans, the same clause RAAS.RENIN.PRESSURE_THRESHOLD already invokes from this same paper. TIER B RATHER THAN THE THRESHOLD ROW'S A, deliberately: the threshold 93 +/- 2 comes from the full 30-study dose-response meta-analysis, while this slope is quoted only for the 5-comparison healthy-versus-hypertensive subset (Figure 6). The paper gives no numeric slope for the 30-study analysis in text - Figure 4 would have to be digitised, which is a different extraction_method. The paper also states 'Risk of bias was high in most studies.' || VALIDITY RANGE. The linear regression was fitted below 90 mmHg renal arterial pressure; the plateau was averaged above 105; the threshold is their intersection. This model runs at MAP 82-87, INSIDE the fitted linear range, so no extrapolation is involved. The pre-existing simplification that systemic MAP is used directly as renal perfusion pressure is unchanged by this row and is Raas.jl's, not this row's. || WHAT IT CHANGES, MEASURED with bench/renin_gain_sweep.jl. Resting pra falls 2.31 -> 1.30 relative to the plateau. THE SALT-STEP STEADY STATE DOES NOT MOVE: escape drives fr_mod to zero, and a 16-fold change in this gain moves the shift by at most 0.81%, so the headline 5.0570 mmHg is unchanged to five significant figures. THE STEADY STATE WITH ESCAPE SUPPRESSED DOES MOVE, and that is ADR 0015's configuration: the fall in the salt-step shift goes from 50.7% at 19.0 to about 22% here. ADR 0015 stays LIVE by its own pre-registered 20% rule and its magnitude more than halves. || DECLARED STRUCTURAL LIMITATION, branch S2 of the pre-registration, and it is NOT a defect in this value. The rectified linear form caps the PRA ratio it can produce between two pressures at the ratio of their drives, independently of the gain. van den Bosch 2021 (PMID 34921521, n = 70 healthy men) reports PRA 2.10 on high salt against 5.74 on low, a ratio of 2.73, at MAP 88 against 86 - where this form's ceiling is (93-86)/(93-88) = 1.40. NO VALUE OF THIS GAIN REPRODUCES THAT. Human salt-induced renin runs mostly through macula densa sodium delivery and renal sympathetic traffic, neither of which this component has. The pre-registration forbade fitting to those data for exactly this reason, and the gap is recorded in HANDOVER section 7 rather than absorbed into this number - which is how RN.PRESSURE_NATRIURESIS.SLOPE became a hypertensive value (section 3.3).

name: Additive fractional sodium reabsorption per unit aldosterone

name: Direct angiotensin II tubular sodium reabsorption, per unit normalised renin activity
citation: Hall JE, Granger JP, Hester RL, Coleman TG, Smith MJ Jr, Cross RB. Mechanisms of escape from sodium retention during angiotensin II hypertension. Am J Physiol 1984;246(5 Pt 2):F627-F634.
notes: SOURCED 2026-09-19 FROM HALL 1984, FULL TEXT READ, angii_tubular_prereg.md. PMID 6720967. Twelve conscious male mongrel dogs 21-27 kg (mean 22.2 +/- 0.8), chronically instrumented, sodium-deficient diet plus supplement to about 80 meq/day, ANG II [Asp1,Val5] at 5 ng/kg/min. EIGHT DOGS HAD RENAL PERFUSION PRESSURE SERVO-CONTROLLED AT THE CONTROL LEVEL by an inflatable aortic occluder driven by a proportional servo-control unit, 24 h a day. That preparation is the whole reason this row is possible: it excludes the pressure-natriuresis route by construction, and it cannot be performed in a human. Directive 1.15. || THE MAGNITUDE IS THE DAY-6 RATE AND NOT THE SIX-DAY AVERAGE. Cumulative sodium balance rose 210 +/- 37 meq over 6 days, which is 35 meq/day averaged - but that average is FRONT-LOADED over a transient the free arm shows directly (Table 1: UNaV falls to 20 meq/day on day 1 and recovers). At day 6 the servo arm excreted 56 +/- 5 meq/day against an intake of about 80, so the ONGOING retention is 24 +/- 5 meq/day. TWO SIGNIFICANT FIGURES, directive 1.13. || WHY THE DAY 6 POINT IS THE RIGHT ONE FOR A NON-ESCAPING TERM: at that point the renal perfusion pressure is STILL CLAMPED, so the pressure route is excluded by the preparation; plasma aldosterone has RETURNED TO CONTROL, 4.9 +/- 0.8 against a control of 4.6 +/- 1.0, so the aldosterone route is excluded BY MEASUREMENT rather than by assumption; and retention continues anyway. What is left is the direct tubular action of angiotensin II, which is exactly what ADR 0015 defines fr_angii to be. || AND HALL CONFIRMS ADR 0015'S STRUCTURAL CHOICE INDEPENDENTLY. His conclusion is that a rise in renal arterial pressure is ESSENTIAL for escape; releasing the occluder took urinary sodium from 56 to 322 +/- 35 meq/day in one day. So escape is PRESSURE-MEDIATED and not intrinsic to the tubular effect, which is why this term is added OUTSIDE the aldosterone escape state rather than inside it. The design was right before the source was found. || THE DERIVATION. Expressed as a fraction of the filtered load, which is intensive: 24 meq/day / (81.5 ml/min = 117.4 L/day x 142.5 meq/l = 16724 meq/day) = 0.00144. Anchored on Hall's own statement that the 5 ng/kg/min dose was calculated to reach plasma ANG II levels found during SODIUM DEPRIVATION, which on this model's pra axis is the low-salt arm: pra 2.5795 at 38 mEq/day against a resting 1.2956, a difference of 1.2839. So k_angii = 0.00144 / 1.2839 = 0.0011 per unit pra, TWO FIGURES. || SCALING: THE TRANSFER IS DONE ON THE FRACTION AND NOT ON THE RATE. A retention in meq/day is EXTENSIVE and would need a body-size scaling to cross species; a fraction of the filtered load is INTENSIVE and does not. That is the same argument RAAS.RENIN.SYMPATHETIC_THRESHOLD_SHIFT makes for an intensive pressure. It is the strongest transfer available and it is still dog to human, which this row states rather than hides. || THREE WEAK LINKS, NAMED IN THE PRE-REGISTRATION BEFORE ANY VALUE WAS ENTERED. (1) The cross-species fractional transfer above. (2) Mapping SODIUM DEPRIVATION onto this model's 38 mEq/day arm is THIS REPOSITORY'S JUDGEMENT AND NOT HALL'S - he names the physiological state, not a pra. (3) Hall's preparation has EXOGENOUS ANG II with SUPPRESSED ENDOGENOUS RENIN, plasma renin activity falling 0.27 to 0.04 ng/ml/h, and this model's pra conflates renin with angiotensin II and cannot represent that dissociation; the anchor therefore rests on total angiotensin II activity being comparable, not on the renin state matching. || NOT FITTED TO ANYTHING THIS MODEL IS JUDGED BY. ADR 0015 requires that the magnitude never be fitted to salt data, and it was not: it comes from a servo-controlled dog preparation at fixed pressure. Hall 1980's clamp contrast - control dogs taking under 7 mmHg across 5 to 500 meq/day against AngII-clamped dogs taking +42 percent - is ADR 0015's FALSIFIABLE TEST and was deliberately kept out of the estimation. || SPECIES: DOG, conscious, chronically instrumented, n = 8 in the servo arm. FULL TEXT READ - supplied by the owner on 2026-09-19, which is what made this row possible after the 2026-09-18 search recorded the mapping as the precise blocker. || THE ESTIMATION COHORT IS MALE - twelve conscious male mongrel dogs - and this row is entered as 'both' because it is a dimensionless fraction of the filtered load with no sexed input, not because the cohort was mixed. No sex difference in the direct tubular action of angiotensin II was sought or found here. name: Urinary osmoles per mEq of sodium excreted
citation: Imamura T, Kinugawa K, Minatsuki S, Muraoka H, Kato N, Inaba T, Maki H, Shiga T, Hatano M, Yao A, Kyo S, Komuro I. Urine osmolality estimated using urine urea nitrogen, sodium and creatinine can effectively predict response to tolvaptan in decompensated heart failure patients. Circ J 2013;77(5):1208-1213. PMID 23318562. The validated estimator carries urine sodium with a coefficient of 2.
notes: THE COEFFICIENT IS ELECTRONEUTRALITY, NOT A FITTED CONSTANT. Every sodium ion leaving in the urine leaves with an accompanying anion, predominantly chloride, so one mEq of excreted sodium contributes approximately two milliosmoles - one for the cation and one for the anion. That is why the standard urine osmolality estimators all carry urine sodium with a coefficient of 2. WHAT THE CITATION ACTUALLY SUPPLIES. Imamura 2013 validated the whole estimator 1.07*(2*[urine Na] + [urine urea nitrogen]/2.8 + [urine creatinine]*2/3) + 16 against MEASURED urine osmolality in 66 patients and reports r = 0.938, p < 0.001. The paper does not measure this coefficient; it measures that a formula containing it reproduces the real thing. That is the honest description of the evidence and is why this row is tier B rather than A. DECLARED LIMITATION OF THE COHORT: decompensated heart failure patients receiving tolvaptan, i.e. a diseased population under a V2 antagonist. Directive 1.7 test - had the correlation come out poorly, the conclusion would have been that estimated urine osmolality cannot predict tolvaptan response, so the composition relation is the INSTRUMENT there and not the subject. It is accepted anyway because the coefficient is not an empirical finding of that paper but a charge-balance requirement, and the validation is corroboration that the requirement holds in real urine. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION OF THE STRUCTURE, not pooled with it: Alwis US, Delanghe J, Dossche L, Walle JV, Van Camp J, Monaghan TF, Roggeman S, Everaert K. Could evening dietary protein intake play a role in nocturnal polyuria? J Clin Med 2020;9(8):2532. PMID 32764521. 170 subjects, 24 h collections in 8 timed samples with volume, osmolality, creatinine, urea and sodium all measured; reports urea as the largest single contributor to urine osmolality with sodium excretion the other major term. That is the two-part structure this row and RN.URINE.SOLUTE_NONNA implement. || ROUNDED 2026-09-09 TO MEASUREMENT PRECISION at the owner's instruction. Nothing physiological in this model is measured to more than four significant figures, and trailing zeros on a whole number read as precision that is not there. The discarded digits were floating-point residue from the derivation, not information. Directive 1.13.

name: Non-sodium urinary solute load, held constant
citation: Derived from RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD, RN.URINE.OSM_PER_NA and BF.NA.INTAKE_NOMINAL.
notes: DERIVED, and it is a RESIDUAL rather than a measurement: SOLUTE_NONNA = RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD - RN.URINE.OSM_PER_NA * BF.NA.INTAKE_MID = 600.0 - 2.0 * 154.0 = 292.0 mOsm/day. It stands for urea plus potassium salts plus everything else, all held constant. WHY IT IS DEFINED THIS WAY. RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD is load-bearing: ADH.URINE.OSM_MAX, ADH.URINE.OSM_BASELINE and ADH.OSM.SENSITIVITY are all derived from it and four closure checks depend on it. Making the solute load track sodium must therefore leave the REFERENCE load untouched, or every derived ADH constant and every steady state moves. Pinning the residual so that total load returns exactly 600.0 at the mid salt arm (154 mEq/day) achieves that: the mid arm is unchanged to the last digit and only the high and low arms move. INHERITED DEBT, STATED PLAINLY: 292 mOsm/day is almost certainly TOO LOW for the non-sodium fraction. Urea alone is normally the largest single contributor to urine osmolality (Alwis 2020) and potassium salts add roughly another 100-120 mOsm/day, so a real non-sodium remainder on a Western diet is nearer 400-500. The residual is small because the parent RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD = 600 mOsm/day is itself an unsourced conventional figure that is low for a 154 mEq/day sodium intake - typical measured totals are 700-900. THIS ROW DOES NOT FIX THAT AND MUST NOT BE READ AS FIXING IT. Correcting the total would move U_max, U_base, k_adh and every steady state, and needs its own pre-registered extraction. What this row does is make the load RESPOND to salt, which it previously did not do at all. Tier C, inherited from the parent. || ROUNDED 2026-09-09 TO MEASUREMENT PRECISION at the owner's instruction. Nothing physiological in this model is measured to more than four significant figures, and trailing zeros on a whole number read as precision that is not there. The discarded digits were floating-point residue from the derivation, not information. Directive 1.13. || RE-DERIVED 2026-09-16 AGAINST THE SOURCED TOTAL, AND THE PIN MOVED FROM THE MID ARM TO THE NOMINAL ARM. 930 - 2*205 = 520 mOsm/day. It was 292, pinned so the total returned 600 at 154 mEq/day while the model runs at 205 - see the Half A note on RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD. || THE INHERITED DEBT THIS ROW DECLARED IS NOW DISCHARGED. Its own text said 292 was 'almost certainly TOO LOW', that urea is normally the largest single contributor and potassium salts add another 100-120 mOsm/day, and that a real remainder is 'nearer 400-500'. Kitada measures urea at 4.1 and potassium at 1.1 mmol/kg/day, which at 83 kg is 340 mOsm/day of urea and 182 of potassium salts. || IT IS STILL A RESIDUAL AND IT IS STILL HELD CONSTANT, AND THE SECOND HALF OF THAT IS NOW MEASURABLY WRONG. In the source the non-sodium remainder FALLS from 7.08 to 6.58 mOsm/kg/day as salt goes 6 -> 12 g/day, because urine urea concentration falls 13.9 percent - the natriuretic-ureotelic pattern the paper is about. So the true slope of total osmolar excretion against excreted sodium is about 1.5 mOsm/mEq, where this model uses 2.0 and holds the rest fixed. ACROSS ITS OWN SALT ARMS THE MODEL THEREFORE OVER-RESPONDS ON THE SOLUTE LIMB BY ROUGHLY 30 PERCENT: 204 mOsm/day of swing from 205 to 103 mEq/day where the data imply about 157. Not built, because the dependence would need a urea-recycling or glucocorticoid mechanism with no sourced form and this pass pre-registered none. It is now a NUMBER rather than an unknown.

name: Non-sodium urinary solute response to sodium excretion
citation: Kitada K, Daub S, Zhang Y, Klein JD, Nakano D, Pedchenko T, Lantier L, LaRocque LM, Marton A, Neubert P, Schroeder A, Rakova N, Jantsch J, Dikalova AE, Dikalov SI, Harrison DG, Mueller DN, Nishiyama A, Rauh M, Harris RC, Luft FC, Wassermann DH, Sands JM, Titze J. OPEN ACCESS, FULL TEXT READ - it is already the citation on RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD. 10 healthy men, 739 complete 24 h collections. THE NON-SODIUM REMAINDER FALLS FROM 7.08 TO 6.58 mOsm/kg/day as salt intake goes 6 -> 12 g/day NaCl, because urine urea concentration falls 13.9 percent - the natriuretic-ureotelic pattern the paper is about.
notes: DERIVED FROM TWO REPORTED VALUES. -0.50 mOsm/kg/day across a 102 mmol/day change in salt intake gives -0.004902, entered as -0.0049. TWO SIGNIFICANT FIGURES AND NOT MORE: the inputs are 7.08 and 6.58, three figures each, and their DIFFERENCE of 0.50 carries two. Directive 1.13. || WHAT IT FIXES. OUTSIDE THAT RANGE IT IS AN EXTRAPOLATION, and the model's own arms - 103 to 205 mmol/day - sit inside it by construction, because they ARE 6 and 12 g/day. || EXTENSIVE, PER KILOGRAM, because urea production tracks lean mass, exactly as RN.URINE.SOLUTE_NONNA already scales. At the 70 kg reference this is -0.343 mOsm/day per mEq/day, so the NET slope of total osmolar excretion against sodium becomes 2.0 - 0.343 = 1.66 against the earlier note's rough estimate of 1.5. || IT IS ZERO AT THE REFERENCE BY CONSTRUCTION. The term is k*(Na_excr - Na_excr_ref), so RN.URINE.SOLUTE_LOAD returns exactly 930 mOsm/day at nominal intake and every ADH constant derived from that total is untouched. validation/solute_limb_prereg.md branch U2: if any of them moves, the TERM is written wrongly and the term gets fixed, not the constants. || RN.URINE.OSM_PER_NA STAYS 2.0. name: Resting heart rate, supine
citation: Gonzales TI, Jeon JY, Lindsay T, Westgate K, Perez-Pozuelo I, Hollidge S, Wijndaele K, Rennie K, Forouhi N, Griffin S, Wareham N, Brage S. Resting heart rate is a population-level biomarker of cardiorespiratory fitness: the Fenland Study. PLoS One 2023;18(5):e0285272.
notes: PRECISION: rounded to 2 significant figures on 2026-08-27. The sources do not support more, and carrying digits that do not exist forced the closure gate and the test suite to chase arithmetic noise. Derived rows inherit the significant figures of their inputs and are rounded to match; the closure tolerance was moved to 1e-3 in the same change, which is still an order of magnitude tighter than the 6% error that motivated that gate. || SUPINE resting heart rate. The Fenland Study reports a POOLED supine mean of 63.5 +/- 8.9 bpm across 10865 adults aged 29-65 (5722 women, 5143 men), and separately that 'on average, RHR was 3 bpm higher in women compared to men'. Solving those two statements with the exact group sizes gives male 61.9201 and female 64.9201. DERIVED, not read off: the paper does not tabulate sex-stratified supine means in the text, so this is arithmetic on two reported quantities. CAVEAT, RECORDED: the 3 bpm sentence says 'RHR' without naming a posture, and the paper reports three (seated 67.6, supine 63.5, sleeping 56.9). It is applied to supine here because supine is the posture this model uses, but if the difference is in fact a seated or pooled-across-posture figure the split is misattributed. The POOLED value is solid; the SPLIT carries this caveat. SUPINE IS THE POSTURE THE MODEL NEEDS: CV.CO.NOMINAL is itself derived from the conventional resting 5 L/min, which is a supine figure. Measured by chest sensor after at least 1 h rest, value taken from the final 3 min of a 6 min recording - a better-defined resting condition than a clinic pulse. COHORT: general population recruited from GP lists in Cambridgeshire, NOT health-screened. Uncertainty carries the POOLED SD; the paper gives no sex-stratified SD. CORROBORATION SEARCHED FOR AND NOT FOUND, recorded so it is not re-searched: three query families over resting heart rate by sex - reference/normal values, sex-differences, and population cohorts - returned risk-association studies (RHR as a predictor of stroke, cancer mortality, atrial fibrillation) rather than reference-value studies reporting sex-stratified resting means. This is a SINGLE-SOURCE pair and pooling.md rule 6 applies: say so, do not dress it as consensus. It is still better than the shared male-nominal value it replaces, because the pairing rule makes the female case explicit rather than implicit. || ROUNDED 2026-09-09 TO MEASUREMENT PRECISION at the owner's instruction. Nothing physiological in this model is measured to more than four significant figures, and trailing zeros on a whole number read as precision that is not there. The discarded digits were floating-point residue from the derivation, not information. Directive 1.13.

citation: Petersen SE, Aung N, Sanghvi MM, Zemrak F, Fung K, Paiva JM, Francis JM, Khanji MY, Lukaschuk E, Lee AM, Carapella V, Kim YJ, Leeson P, Piechnik SK, Neubauer S. Reference ranges for cardiac structure and function using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) in Caucasians from the UK Biobank population cohort. J Cardiovasc Magn Reson 2017;19(1):18.
notes: SOURCED 2026-09-01, AND THE DEPENDENCY NOW RUNS THE WAY THE MEASUREMENT DOES. Was 80.7 / 77.0 mL, DERIVED from CV.CO.NOMINAL and CV.HR.NOMINAL - a measured quantity computed from an `assumed` one whose citation was empty. Pre-re-registered in validation/dependency_inversion_prereg.md, which was committed BEFORE any paper was opened and sits immediately before this change in main's history. NO COMMIT SHA IS CITED, DELIBERATELY - rebase-merge rewrites it and every such citation already in this ledger points at a commit main does not contain. Verify the ordering instead: git log --diff-filter=A -- validation/dependency_inversion_prereg.md. HANDOVER section 4 item 1. NOW REPORTED: Petersen 2017, UK Biobank CMR. Left ventricular stroke volume 96 +/- 20 mL in 368 men. Cohort: 804 participants remaining after exclusion for non-Caucasian ethnicity, known cardiovascular disease and any condition affecting chamber size or function, of whom 800 (368 men, 432 women) have ventricular measurements. Ages 45-74. SINGLE SOURCE, k = 1, pooling.md rule 6 - stated plainly and not dressed as consensus. TECHNIQUE, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS NOT INTERCHANGEABLE. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance, steady-state free precession at 1.5 T, manual contouring, PAPILLARY MUSCLES AND TRABECULATIONS INCLUDED IN THE LV VOLUME. Zhan 2024 (Circ Cardiovasc Imaging 2024;17(2):e016090, 254 studies screened, 12,812 healthy adults) exists because that convention moves LV volumes, and it pools the two conventions SEPARATELY rather than across them. pooling.md prohibits pooling across incompatible measurement methods, so this row is single-source BY RULE and not by neglect. WHAT WAS SCREENED AND WHY IT WAS NOT USED, so the next attempt does not repeat it. (1) Zhan 2024, the meta-analysis pooling.md rule 1 would have preferred: reports lower and upper reference LIMITS, indexed to body surface area. range-midpoint is prohibited for new entries and the model carries no BSA, so it fails twice. (2) Luu 2022, Canadian Alliance for Healthy Hearts and Minds (J Cardiovasc Magn Reson 2022;24(1):2), n = 3206, multi-ethnic, anatomically correct contouring - LARGER AND BETTER DESIGNED THAN THE ROW ADOPTED, and reports LVSV INDEXED ONLY (46 +/- 8 male, 42 +/- 7 female mL/m2). Converting it needs a BSA formula, which this model does not carry and which the pre-registration explicitly refused to introduce as a side effect. It also contours papillary muscles into LV MASS rather than volume, so it could not be pooled with Petersen in any case. (3) Patel 2021 WASE (PMID 34044105) paywalled, no numbers in the abstract - recorded against CV.CO.NOMINAL since 2026-08-31 and still unopened. (4) Addetia 2022 WASE 3D echo (J Am Soc Echocardiogr 2022;35(5):449-459), n = 1589 - indexed only, and 3D echo is a different technique. (5) Salton 2002 Framingham Offspring (n = 142) and Le Ven 2016 (n = 434, mean age 26) - both report the direction but not absolute stroke volume in the record read. NOT NORMALISED TO THE REFERENCE MASS, AND THAT IS RECORDED DEBT RATHER THAN A CHOICE. This value is EXTENSIVE and is multiplied by size_factor = body_mass / BF.BODY_MASS.REFERENCE, so it should be stated at 70 kg. Petersen reports body weight by AGE GROUP (71, 71, 69 kg) but NOT by sex, so the cohort mean is essentially the reference mass while the male and female subgroups plainly are not. The pre-registration fixed the rule in advance: normalise where cohort mass is reported by sex, otherwise enter as reported and record the mismatch. So this pair still carries a body-size component, and in the ensemble - where mass is sampled by sex - that component is counted twice. Fixing it needs sex-stratified cohort mass or a BSA row. AND THE PREDICTION FIXED IN ADVANCE WAS HALF WRONG, WHICH IS THE USEFUL PART. The previous note on this row cited Katori 1979 for NO significant sex difference in stroke INDEX and concluded the dimorphism is body size, not the heart. Petersen indexes to BSA and the difference SURVIVES: 49 +/- 10 male against 45 +/- 8 female mL/m2, a 9% male excess where the absolute difference is 28%. Luu 2022 finds the same on 3206 people (46 vs 42), Salton 2002 states volumetric measures remain greater in men after BSA adjustment, and Le Ven 2016 states all gender differences remained after normalisation. Four independent cohorts. So body size carries roughly two thirds of the difference and about a third is not size - the pair was expected to collapse the way ECF per kg did when blood volume and haematocrit were sourced, and it does not. || ROUNDED 2026-09-09 TO MEASUREMENT PRECISION at the owner's instruction. Nothing physiological in this model is measured to more than four significant figures, and trailing zeros on a whole number read as precision that is not there. The discarded digits were floating-point residue from the derivation, not information. Directive 1.13. || DE-INDEXED 2026-09-16, deindexing_prereg.md Stage 2, AND IT NEEDED NO NEW SOURCE. 96 -> 89 mL (male), 75 -> 79 (female). Petersen reports the SAME cohort both ways - absolute 96 and 75 mL, indexed 49 +/- 10 and 45 +/- 8 mL/m2 - so the implied cohort body surface area is their quotient: 1.959 m2 in the men and 1.667 in the women. The model's reference individual has 1.824 and 1.751. The entered value is now the indexed figure at the model's own reference body, 49 x 1.824 and 45 x 1.751, at the two significant figures the indexed pair carries. || THIS ROW DESCRIBED ITS OWN DEFECT AND THE FIX IS THE ONE IT ASKED FOR. Its previous note: 'this pair still carries a body-size component, and in the ensemble - where mass is sampled by sex - that component is counted twice. Fixing it needs sex-stratified cohort mass or a BSA row.' The BSA row landed on 2026-09-05 and did nothing for eleven days. || THE PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION HELD, AND IT COULD HAVE FAILED. deindexing_prereg.md section 6 fixed in advance that the male value must move DOWN and the female UP, because the reference mass is 70 kg for both sexes - light for a man, heavy for a woman. Measured: -6.9 and +5.0 percent. Had both moved the same way the reference BSA pair would have been wrong and branch B5 would have stopped the stage. || AND IT HALVES THE APPARENT SEX DIFFERENCE. The absolute pair carried 28 percent, of which Petersen's own indexing says 9 percent survives body size. This pair carries 13 percent - the indexed 9 plus the 4 percent difference in reference surface area, which is height alone at a shared 70 kg. The rest was Petersen's men being larger than Petersen's women, which the ensemble was already counting through sexed mass sampling. || WHAT IS UNCHANGED: the source, the cohort, the technique and the screening record. Luu 2022 is still unusable - it contours papillary muscles into LV MASS rather than volume, so it cannot be pooled with Petersen whatever the indexing - and Zhan 2024 still reports reference LIMITS, which pooling.md prohibits for new entries. HANDOVER section 4 item 10 claimed BSA would unlock both. It unlocks neither.
