name: Fraction of pulse pressure lying BELOW mean pressure
notes: ASSUMED at the conventional one third, which is the familiar MAP = DBP + PP/3. Discharges the TODO in reconstruct.jl, which carried this as a HARDCODED default of 0.4 and demanded a ledger row before the function was used for anything - directive 1.4 is now satisfied. NAME AND JUSTIFICATION CORRECTED 2026-08-27; THE VALUE IS UNCHANGED AND WAS ALWAYS RIGHT. This row was entered as 'Fraction of pulse pressure lying ABOVE mean pressure', and 0.3333 is the fraction lying BELOW it. Against the tier A central pressures in this same ledger - SBP 109, DBP 76, PP 33, MAP 87 - the fraction above the mean is (109-87)/33 = 0.667 and the fraction below is (87-76)/33 = 0.333. The old note's reasoning was inverted in the same way: it said 'the fraction of pulse pressure above mean must be below 0.5 because diastole is longer than systole', and diastole being longer is exactly why MAP sits NEARER DIASTOLIC, which makes the fraction BELOW the mean the one that must be under 0.5. The 0.515 that exposed the brachial/central mixing was (93-76)/33, a below-mean fraction, so the impossibility argument itself was correct and only its label was wrong. WHY IT MATTERED. check_closure.py uses this row as MAP = DBP + k*PP, i.e. with the CORRECT below-mean meaning, and passes. reconstruct.jl defined its form_factor as the fraction ABOVE the mean and computed SBP = MAP + form_factor*PP. Wiring the ledger row into that function under the shared name 'form factor' would have produced SBP 98.0 and DBP 65.0 against the sourced 109 and 76 - both wrong by PP/3 = 11 mmHg, in opposite directions - and NO GATE WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT, because the closure check never reaches reconstruct.jl. Found while connecting that file, not by any check. reconstruct.jl now takes k_below explicitly and names the convention in its signature. NOT CONSTANT IN REALITY, and reconstruct.jl calls treating it as constant the single largest error source in the reconstruction: it varies with heart rate, arterial stiffness, disease state, and - as the 87 versus 89.8 discrepancy shows - with measurement site. name: Oxygen bound per gram of haemoglobin

name: Severinghaus dissociation coefficient A
citation: Severinghaus JW. Simple, accurate equations for human blood O2 dissociation computations. J Appl Physiol Respir Environ Exerc Physiol 1979;46(3):599-602. doi:10.1152/jappl.1979.46.3.599. PMID 35496. ABSTRACT READ - the equation and its stated accuracy are both in the abstract, which is the part used. The paper fits the STANDARD HUMAN BLOOD O2 dissociation curve to within +/- 0.0055 fractional saturation over 0 < S < 1.
notes: ONE OF TWO COEFFICIENTS OF A SINGLE PUBLISHED FIT. S = 1/(A/(PO2^3 + B*PO2) + 1). THEY ARE NOT SEPARATELY MEASURABLE AND MUST MOVE TOGETHER OR NOT AT ALL - neither has a physical meaning on its own, and changing one without the other produces a curve nobody published. || BRANCH B3 OF validation/blood_gas_prereg.md, AND THE PRE-REGISTRATION PREFERRED OTHERWISE. Section 4 preferred the Hill form because its two parameters - P50 and the exponent - are separately measurable and would get separate rows with separate provenance. THE DECOMPOSITION FAILED: searching for a measured P50 and Hill exponent in healthy humans returns chronic obstructive lung disease, sickle cell disease, chronic hypoxaemia, sleep apnoea and congenital heart disease, every one excluded by section 2, several of them existing to characterise a pulse oximeter rather than the physiology (directive 1.7). So a published fit is taken whole, with its citation and its stated error, and the loss of decomposability is the recorded cost. || A PUBLISHED EQUATION FITTED TO MEASURED DATA IS NOT ANOTHER MODEL'S OUTPUT, which is the distinction validation/targets.md draws and the reason this is admissible at all. || THE IMPLIED P50 IS 26.86 Torr, SOLVED FROM THE EQUATION AND DELIBERATELY NOT A LEDGER ROW, so it cannot silently disagree with the curve it comes from. check_closure.py asserts it lands in the human range, which makes it a TEST of the adopted equation rather than a second definition of the same quantity. Severinghaus's own Bohr equation uses PO2/26.6 as its reference, so 26.86 is consistent with the paper to within 1 percent. || FIXED AT NORMAL pH AND TEMPERATURE. ADR 0018 records what that disqualifies: the Bohr effect, fever and hypothermia, 2,3-DPG, and the increased offloading in exercising muscle. pH needs bicarbonate, which is renal and absent. || INTENSIVE.

name: Alveolar-arterial oxygen difference, young adult
citation: NOT SOURCED. The correct source was identified and could not be opened: Crapo RO, Jensen RL, Hegewald M, Tashkin DP. Arterial blood gas reference values for sea level and an altitude of 1,400 meters. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 1999;160(5 Pt 1):1525-31. doi:10.1164/ajrccm.160.5.9806006. PMID 10556115. name: Fall in log-e thyrotropin per unit free thyroxine
citation: DERIVED, and it had to become derived. b = THY.LOOP_GAIN / THY.FT4.EUTHYROID = 2.277 / 10.16, because a slope in units of 1/(pmol/L) is SCALE-DEPENDENT and the model's free thyroxine is now on the NHANES immunoassay scale. The measured slopes it comes from are on other scales and cannot be transferred directly. Sources behind the loop gain: Benhadi N, Fliers E, Visser TJ, Reitsma JB, Wiersinga WM. Eur J Endocrinol 2010;162(2):323-9. PMID 19926783, ABSTRACT ONLY, n = 21 healthy volunteers under randomised T4 and T3 loading - a WITHIN-SUBJECT PERTURBATION, which is the design a feedback gain needs. Reported log TSH = 1.50 - 0.059 x FT4, base 10 (see validation/thyroid_extract.py section 1). || AND Jostel A, Ryder WDJ, Shalet SM. Clin Endocrinol (Oxf) 2009;71(4):529-34. PMID 19226261, ABSTRACT ONLY, 9519 tests in 4064 patients, 0.1345 per pmol/L in natural-log units, combined with the free-thyroxine mean of the cohort that applies it in Wang Y et al. Front Endocrinol (Lausanne) 2021;12:657114, PMC8129566, OPEN ACCESS, read in full.
notes: THE FEEDBACK GAIN OF THE HUMAN THYROID AXIS, in natural-log units per pmol/L of free thyroxine. Benhadi's 0.059 read as base 10 is 0.059*ln(10) = 0.13585; Jostel's is 0.1345. THE TWO AGREE TO 1% AND ONLY UNDER THAT PAIRING - read Benhadi as ln and the two competent measurements of the same gain differ 2.3-fold, in cohorts of comparable FT4 range, which is not credible. || THE VALUE ENTERED IS BENHADI'S because that cohort is admissible under thyroid_prereg.md section 2 on every criterion and the design is an intervention; Jostel's population is a hypopituitary referral series and its purpose was to define a diagnostic index, which is directive 1.7's flag. It is the corroboration, not the value. NOT POOLED - different assays, and pooling.md forbids pooling across incompatible methods. The uncertainty range is the two estimates, not a confidence interval. || THIS ROW DISCHARGES BRANCH T3, which an earlier extraction pass took correctly on the evidence then available. || VALUE CHANGED 2026-09-05, AND THE CHANGE IS THE POINT. This row first entered Benhadi's 0.13585 alone and called Jostel's 0.1345 'corroboration, not the value', on the grounds that pooling.md forbids pooling across assays. THE TWO NUMBERS DIFFER BY 1%. Choosing between measurements that agree to within a fifth of any plausible experimental error is not rigour, it is a coin toss dressed as a decision - directive 1.9 and HANDOVER section 3.23, both of which this repository already had. The entered value is now the MEAN of the two, 0.1352, and the uncertainty is their spread. || UNWEIGHTED, because neither source reports a standard error and the weights cannot change a 1% interval by anything that matters. Method: two estimates, arithmetic mean; extraction_method is therefore derived rather than reported, since no paper prints 0.1352. || WHAT THE SPREAD IS WORTH, and it is the useful consequence: carrying both ends through the loop moves the predicted euthyroid thyrotropin from 3.32 to 3.39 mIU/L, about 2%. So the slope is NOT where the model's 2.4x thyrotropin discrepancy comes from, and that is now arithmetic rather than assertion. || WHY THIS ROW MOVED, AND IT IS A UNIT ERROR RATHER THAN AN IMPRECISE NUMBER. The ledger previously composed a pituitary line measured on one free-thyroxine assay (Benhadi 2010) with a free-thyroxine concentration measured by equilibrium dialysis (Braverman 1973), and predicted a euthyroid thyrotropin 2.2x the measured population value. THE TWO SCALES ARE NOT COMMENSURATE AND THAT IS NOW MEASURED: at essentially identical TOTAL thyroxine - 7.75 ug/dL in NHANES against Braverman's 7.30, agreeing to 6% - the free fraction is 0.0104% by immunoassay against 0.0180% by dialysis, a ratio of 1.73. Two methods agreeing on the total hormone to a few per cent and disagreeing by nearly two-fold on the free fraction are not two measurements of one quantity. thyroid_prereg.md section 2 prohibited POOLING across free-thyroxine assays and should have prohibited COMPOSING across them too. || THE PREVIOUS VALUE, 0.1352, WAS THE MEAN OF TWO MEASURED SLOPES ON TWO OTHER ASSAYS, and entering it against a third assay's concentration is what produced the 2.2x error. The dimensionless product b*FT4* is scale-invariant and is what actually transfers; it is now its own row. || The range is THY.LOOP_GAIN's range divided by the same concentration.

name: Log-e thyrotropin extrapolated to zero free thyroxine
citation: DERIVED. a = ln(THY.TSH.EUTHYROID) + THY.LOOP_GAIN = ln(1.512) + 2.277. Sources are those two rows; nothing new is sourced here.
notes: THE LOAD-BEARING WEAKNESS OF THIS AXIS, AND IT IS SAID HERE RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER. The slope has two independent estimates agreeing to 1% and the euthyroid FT4 has two agreeing to within a standard deviation; THIS NUMBER HAS ONE SOURCE AND IT CARRIES THE WHOLE OF THE MODEL'S DISCREPANCY IN THYROTROPIN. Reconstructing it from independent euthyroid pairs at the agreed slope gives 2.72 (Maushart euthyroid visit), 2.82 (Maushart 3-month) and 2.59 (NHANES III geometric mean TSH at the sourced FT4) - all 0.6 to 0.9 log units below 3.454, a factor of 1.9-2.4 in TSH. || WHY IT WOULD BE HIGH, AND THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF THE SAME PATTERN IN THIS REPOSITORY: an intercept is a line extrapolated to FT4 = 0 from data that never approached zero. The same extrapolation forced the ADR 0017 amendment - a chemoreflex line extrapolated below its measured range put ventilation at 19.3 L/min against a real 6.2 - and produced HANDOVER section 3.22's censoring bound. Benhadi's cohort is also mean age 60 and NHANES III reports TSH rising with age. || IT IS NOT REPLACED BY ANY OF THE RECONSTRUCTIONS. Every one of them is built from a measured euthyroid TSH, which is the quantity ADR 0019's falsifiable test 2 judges the loop against; fitting to it would be HANDOVER section 3.15's error committed deliberately. The model reports a euthyroid TSH 2.4x the NHANES III geometric mean and nothing downstream consumes TSH. || CUT FROM 3.453878 TO 3.454 ON 2026-09-05. Seven significant figures on a number whose source reports three ('1.50') is exactly the false precision directive 1.9 exists to stop. || AND THE ARITHMETIC THAT CONVICTS THIS ROW RATHER THAN THE SLOPE: sweeping the slope across its full two-source spread moves the predicted euthyroid thyrotropin by 2%, against a discrepancy of 2.4x. Nothing about the slope's uncertainty reaches that. The intercept does, because slope and intercept in a regression over a narrow range are strongly anti-correlated and the intercept is the extrapolated one - Benhadi's free-thyroxine range is a euthyroid baseline plus a thyroxine load, and the intercept lies about 17 pmol/L outside it. THE ABSTRACT REPORTS NO STANDARD ERROR FOR IT, so its variance cannot be propagated and the honest statement is that this coefficient is not determined to better than roughly a factor of two by the study that reports it. || THIS ROW WAS THE WHOLE PROBLEM AND IS NO LONGER SOURCED DIRECTLY. It carried Benhadi's 3.454 - one abstract, no standard error, an extrapolation to zero free thyroxine from data that never went near zero - and the model inherited a euthyroid thyrotropin 2.2x too high. NHANES settled what was actually wrong: not the coefficient's precision but the SCALE it was composed against. || WHY THIS ROW MOVED, AND IT IS A UNIT ERROR RATHER THAN AN IMPRECISE NUMBER. The ledger previously composed a pituitary line measured on one free-thyroxine assay (Benhadi 2010) with a free-thyroxine concentration measured by equilibrium dialysis (Braverman 1973), and predicted a euthyroid thyrotropin 2.2x the measured population value. THE TWO SCALES ARE NOT COMMENSURATE AND THAT IS NOW MEASURED: at essentially identical TOTAL thyroxine - 7.75 ug/dL in NHANES against Braverman's 7.30, agreeing to 6% - the free fraction is 0.0104% by immunoassay against 0.0180% by dialysis, a ratio of 1.73. Two methods agreeing on the total hormone to a few per cent and disagreeing by nearly two-fold on the free fraction are not two measurements of one quantity. thyroid_prereg.md section 2 prohibited POOLING across free-thyroxine assays and should have prohibited COMPOSING across them too. || IT IS NOW DERIVED FROM THE OPERATING POINT RATHER THAN THE OTHER WAY ROUND, which is the same dependency inversion ADR 0017 made for arterial PCO2 and for the same reason - derive from the quantity that is actually measured. The consequence is stated plainly on THY.TSH.EUTHYROID: the euthyroid thyrotropin is now an INPUT and ADR 0019's falsifiable test 2 is VOID.

It is checked rather than argued: Maushart's euthyroid immunoassay visits give 15.0 and 16.6 pmol/L. || SEXED PAIR NOT SUPPORTED. Braverman's control group is 11 subjects and no sex-specific values are given; ADR 0014's 'where only one value is supported, use it for both' applies, and this row is the CV.HEMATOCRIT.NOMINAL failure waiting to happen if free thyroxine turns out to be dimorphic. || CUT TO FOUR SIGNIFICANT FIGURES ON 2026-09-05, from 16.605. The source reports 1.29 +/- 0.19 ng/100 mL, three figures; converting a unit does not create a fourth. || WHY THIS ROW MOVED, AND IT IS A UNIT ERROR RATHER THAN AN IMPRECISE NUMBER. The ledger previously composed a pituitary line measured on one free-thyroxine assay (Benhadi 2010) with a free-thyroxine concentration measured by equilibrium dialysis (Braverman 1973), and predicted a euthyroid thyrotropin 2.2x the measured population value. THE TWO SCALES ARE NOT COMMENSURATE AND THAT IS NOW MEASURED: at essentially identical TOTAL thyroxine - 7.75 ug/dL in NHANES against Braverman's 7.30, agreeing to 6% - the free fraction is 0.0104% by immunoassay against 0.0180% by dialysis, a ratio of 1.73. Two methods agreeing on the total hormone to a few per cent and disagreeing by nearly two-fold on the free fraction are not two measurements of one quantity. thyroid_prereg.md section 2 prohibited POOLING across free-thyroxine assays and should have prohibited COMPOSING across them too. || SEX: NO PAIR IS NEEDED, AND THAT IS NOW A FINDING RATHER THAN AN ABSENCE. Free thyroxine differs by 0.5% between men and women in 6814 adults (10.18 against 10.13 pmol/L) and thyrotropin by 3% (1.534 against 1.486). ADR 0014's 'where only one value is supported, use it for both' was previously invoked because no sexed pair could be found; it is now invoked because a large sample says there is nothing to find.

name: Thyroxine turnover time constant
citation: Braverman LE, Vagenakis A, Downs P, Foster AE, Sterling K, Ingbar SH. citation: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2007-2008, 2009-2010 and 2011-2012, public microdata, files THYROD/DEMO/RXQ_RX/MCQ from https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/. name: Fraction of filtered sodium reabsorbed before the macula densa
citation: No admissible source could be opened. See notes.

This fraction sets the SCALE of distal delivery; the macula densa gain multiplies the FRACTIONAL deviation of that delivery from its own reference. Halving one and doubling the other leaves every model output identical. Since the gain is estimated against salt-renin data, only the product is determined, and entering a sourced fraction would buy nothing until the gain is independently measured too. || IT ADDS NO INFORMATION ABOUT SEGMENTAL HANDLING and ADR 0021's disqualification section says so: the split is OBSERVATIONAL - it defines a variable and does not restructure the sodium equation, which is untouched. || RENAMED 2026-09-17: IT WAS CALLED A PROXIMAL FRACTION AND IT IS NOT ONE. Renal.jl computes Na_distal = Na_filtered*(1-this) and feeds it to md_drive, the MACULA DENSA signal. The macula densa sits at the end of the THICK ASCENDING LIMB - after the proximal tubule and after the loop - so 10 percent delivery is proximal PLUS loop combined. A name carrying a convention its value contradicts is HANDOVER section 3.2's failure mode, and this is the third instance. The param_id, the name and the symbol now say which segment this is. || AND IT IS COMPLETELY INERT, WHICH IS STRONGER THAN WHAT THIS ROW USED TO CLAIM. The note said it was 'not separately identifiable from RN.MD.RENIN_GAIN'. It is worse than that: md_drive = (Na_distal_ref - Na_distal)/Na_distal_ref and the factor (1-this) appears in BOTH, so it CANCELS EXACTLY. Only the REPORTED Na_distal moves. || SO SOURCING THIS ROW WOULD BUY NOTHING BEHAVIOURALLY, and that is why it is still assumed after a pass that went looking for it. name: Renin drive per fractional fall in distal sodium delivery
citation: ESTIMATED, NOT MEASURED, and ADR 0021's falsifiable test 1 declared it so before the fact. Solved against van den Bosch JJJON, Hessels NR, Visser FW, Krikken JA, Bakker SJL, Riphagen IJ, Navis GJ. Plasma sodium, extracellular fluid volume, and blood pressure in healthy men. Physiol Rep 2021;9(24):e15103. PMID 34921521. PMC8683787. n = 70 healthy normotensive men, crossover, 7 days per level, intake verified by 24 h urinary sodium at 230 +/- 67 against 38 +/- 26 mmol/24 h, with plasma renin activity 2.10 against 5.74 ng/mL/h.
notes: THE SALT-RENIN DATA ARE NOW AN ESTIMATION SET AND MUST NEVER BE REPORTED AS AGREEMENT. HANDOVER section 3.15 records what happened the last time an estimation set was quoted back as a validation, and the pre-registration wrote this warning twice before the number existed. || WHAT REMAINS A TEST IS THE FORM, NOT THE FIT. HANDOVER section 7 records that the pressure-only rectified relation caps the achievable renin ratio between two pressures at the ratio of their drives - 1.40 between MAP 88 and 86 - whatever the gain, against a measured 2.73. A ceiling either is or is not exceeded, and no value of the OLD gain exceeds it. That the new form can is a structural result; that it lands on 2.73 is arithmetic. || SECOND CALIBRATED ROW IN THE LEDGER, and the first was the pressure-natriuresis slope. That count was zero-bound and is now going the wrong way; it is the price of a mechanism whose gain nobody has measured in a human without moving three other things at once. || RENAL SYMPATHETIC TRAFFIC IS STILL ABSENT. Section 7 names two missing inputs and this adds one, so the estimate absorbs whatever the sympathetic arm would have contributed. That is the same criticism this repository makes of the old pressure gain, made here against its own new row. || NO ORIGINATING MODEL, AND THAT IS WHY THIS SENTENCE EXISTS. SOURCES.md's `calibrated` label was written for values lifted from another model's fitted parameters, and the gate asks such a row to name that model. There is none: this is solved inside THIS model against human measurements, which makes it a fit rather than a citation and is exactly why it carries the label. Naming the absence is the honest answer to a check that assumed the other case. || THE ESTIMATION COHORT IS MALE - 70 healthy normotensive men - and the row is entered `both` because the mechanism is not sexed in anything found and ADR 0014's shared-value branch applies. If the salt-renin response turns out to be dimorphic, this row inherits a male value applied to women, which is the CV.HEMATOCRIT.NOMINAL failure named on that row. || SOLVED BY BISECTION ON THE MODEL ITSELF, 2026-09-05: at g_md = 5.396 the plasma renin ratio between 38 and 230 mmol/day of sodium is 2.7332, matching van den Bosch's 5.74/2.10 to four figures - which is arithmetic, not agreement. AT g_md = 0 THE SAME RATIO IS 1.142, confirming HANDOVER section 7's ceiling directly rather than by argument. || ONLY THE RATIO IS COMPARABLE. This model's plasma renin activity is NORMALISED to 1.0 at the reference individual, not expressed in ng/mL/h, so its absolute values - 2.72 and 0.99 at those two intakes - cannot be compared with van den Bosch's and are not. || THE ARM IS SIGNED WHERE THE PRESSURE ARM IS RECTIFIED, so a large enough distal delivery would drive the renin target negative. The target is now floored at zero in Raas.jl; the floor is inert at every sourced value - the target is 1.05 at the highest intake in the estimation set - and exists because an unphysical negative would otherwise appear only in a regime nobody had looked at. || RE-ESTIMATED THE SAME DAY, 2.480 -> 5.396, AND NOTHING ABOUT THE DATA CHANGED. What changed is the signal this gain reads: the pressure and natriuretic-peptide terms were removed from distal delivery because both are calibrated against sodium excretion and this arm returns to sodium excretion, which counts the same measurement twice. The remaining signal is smaller, so the gain solved against the SAME van den Bosch ratio is larger. ADR 0021 amendment A6 and HANDOVER section 3.32. || THE FAILURE THAT FOUND IT WAS ACUTE, NOT CHRONIC. The chronic salt sensitivity and every resting value were bit-identical with the double count in place, because aldosterone escape zeroes the tubular effect at steady state. Only Lobo's six-hour saline challenge moved, and it moved by a factor of about 1.5. A model whose steady states are all correct can still be wrong about every transient. || RE-SOLVED 2026-09-16, 5.396 -> 5.81, BECAUSE THE WATER LIMB MOVED AND NOT BECAUSE ANY RENIN DATUM DID. The estimation set is unchanged - van den Bosch's 5.74 and 2.10 ng/mL/h at 24 h urinary sodium 38 and 230 mmol/day - and this row is DEFINED as the value that reproduces their ratio, so when anything upstream of renin moves, this number moves with it or it stops being what its own name says. || WHAT MOVED: urine_solute_prereg.md corrected the reference point of the solute load and then sourced it, and ADH.OSM.SENSITIVITY rose 64 percent as a result. That stiffened the osmotic limb, which changed the extracellular volume excursion across the salt arms, which changed renin. Measured: the salt-renin ratio fell 2.733 -> 2.581, a 5.6 percent drop, of which about a third came from Half A alone. || THAT COUPLING IS THE FINDING AND IT WAS NOT PREVIOUSLY QUANTIFIED. A 64 percent change in the osmoregulatory gain moves the salt-renin response by 5.6 percent, so the two limbs are coupled about an order of magnitude less than one for one - which is worth knowing before the next pass touches either. || IT IS STILL A FIT AND MAY NEVER BE REPORTED AS AGREEMENT. Directive 1.13, applied to a row that was already violating it. || RE-SOLVED 2026-09-18, 5.81 -> 5.71, AS A CONSEQUENCE OF THE ADH OSMOTIC MAP PASS (adh_osmotic_map_prereg.md) AND NOT AS A NEW FIT. This row is extraction_method=calibrated and its own note above says it is 'solved inside THIS model against human measurements' - so when the model changes, the solution changes, and leaving it stale would make that sentence false. Sourcing the ADH slope from Baylis 1986 altered the water limb, which feeds ECF volume, which feeds renin; the chronic renin ratio drifted from 2.733 to 2.770, a 1.4 percent excursion that test/runtests.jl caught at rtol 1e-2. || THE TARGET IS UNCHANGED AND THIS IS STILL NOT AGREEMENT. van den Bosch's 5.74 and 2.10 are the same estimation set they always were; re-solving restores an ARITHMETIC identity and reports nothing new. What remains a test is the FORM - that the macula densa arm exceeds the pressure-only ceiling at all - and that is untouched. || NOTHING WAS PHYSIOLOGICALLY WRONG AND NOTHING WAS FIXED - DIRECTIVE 1.13. van den Bosch prints 5.74 and 2.10, so their ratio is about 2.73 and the ROUNDING ALONE spans 2.724-2.743, before any sampling error on a PRA ratio in 70 subjects. THAT MEASUREMENT CANNOT DISTINGUISH 2.77 FROM 2.73. So the drift the test caught was inside the estimation set's own resolution and the value moved in its THIRD SIGNIFICANT FIGURE, which is bookkeeping. What was stale was the INTERNAL IDENTITY - a calibrated row must equal the value that solves the model it is calibrated in - and that is the only reason to touch it. No coupling strength should be read off this 1.7 percent: it is a number about the model's arithmetic, not about physiology. || THE ALTERNATIVE WAS TO WIDEN THE TEST'S TOLERANCE AND IT WAS NOT TAKEN. A calibrated row going stale is fixed by re-solving it, not by loosening the check that noticed. || RE-SOLVED 2026-09-18, 5.71 -> 4.99, BECAUSE THE RENAL SYMPATHETIC ARM NOW SUPPLIES PART OF WHAT THIS GAIN WAS ABSORBING. ADR 0021 decision 7 said in advance that it absorbed the renal sympathetic traffic the model lacked, and A6.3 predicted - before the arm existed - that building that traffic must LOWER this gain. Had the gain NOT fallen, ADR 0021 A6.3 named the successor mechanism in advance - tubuloglomerular feedback on the afferent arteriole - and that branch was live until this ran. || THE TARGET IS UNCHANGED AND THIS IS STILL NOT AGREEMENT. van den Bosch's 5.74 and 2.10 remain the ESTIMATION SET they always were; what changed is how much of the ratio the macula densa has to carry alone. The renal sympathetic arm now built covers only the DIRECT beta-adrenergic threshold shift on renin (Kirchheim 1985). Sympathetic effects on tubular sodium reabsorption and on afferent arteriolar tone are STILL absent, and tubuloglomerular feedback is still not built, so this gain still absorbs those. The number stays 0.884 and the reference individual is bit-identical, which is the point - promoting a constant to a function is a structural change and it is made without moving any existing result. || THE LEVEL IS BRUNNER'S AND THE SLOPE IS HENE'S, AND THE SPLIT IS DELIBERATE. Hene's own level implies 44.6 mmol/day of urinary potassium at ordinary intake against 61.17 measured by 24-hour collection in the nineteen control arms of Cappuccio 2016 - a 27 percent miss - so its level is out of line with everything else while its WITHIN-SUBJECT change is the only admissible measurement of the rise there is. Slope from the within-subject design, level from the population data, and both halves said out loud rather than blended. || D4 KEPT THIS CONSTANT FOR TWO DAYS AND D5 NOW FIRES. The datum that pointed the other way was Cappuccio's MARGINAL fraction, 0.734; the owner struck it out on the ground that it is the fate of a potassium chloride TABLET rather than of food, so tablet absorption and not renal handling sets it. With it gone the sources no longer disagree. || KEPT AS A CONSTANT ON 2026-09-06 BY DECISION D4 OF validation/potassium_doseresponse_prereg.md, NOT BY DEFAULT. Section 5 fixed IN ADVANCE the shape a rising fraction would take, and section 6 branch D5 would have taken it on two or more admissible studies measuring the rise. THE SOURCES DISAGREE ON THE SIGN. D4 says report the disagreement and do not split it. || AND THE MARGINAL FRACTION IS NOT A CLEAN MEASUREMENT OF THE DIETARY ONE: it is the fate of a potassium chloride tablet, not of food, and tablet absorption, incomplete 24-hour collections and trial compliance all push it down with the same sign. Reported because it is what was measured; not used to move this row. || THE PRODUCT OF THIS ROW AND K.INTAKE.NOMINAL IS NOW CHECKED AGAINST SOMETHING, WHICH IT NEVER WAS. 0.884 * 69.06 = 61.05 mmol/day of urinary potassium, against 61.17 measured by 24-hour collection in the 19 control arms of Cappuccio 2016 across 12 countries - 0.2 percent. The residual is stool, which this model does not have. || THE RANGE INCLUDES A VALUE ABOVE 1, which is not an error: those subjects were in negative potassium balance during a load, still excreting stores laid down earlier. A one-compartment model cannot represent that and the range records it. || IT IS A FRACTION, SO IT IS INTENSIVE, and the intake it multiplies already scales. || TWO GOOD GROUPS DISAGREE AND IT IS NOT AVERAGED HERE. This row is a CONSTANT and the human fraction is not: Hene 1986 (PMID 3523191) measured urinary potassium 50 of 80 mEq/day, rising to 233 of 300, so 0.63 -> 0.78; Rabelink 1990 (PMID 2266680) about 0.80 at 400 mmol/day. name: Fraction of filtered sodium leaving the proximal tubule
citation: Shirley DG, Walter SJ, Noormohamed FH. Natriuretic effect of caffeine: assessment of segmental sodium reabsorption in humans. Clin Sci (Lond) 2002;103(5):461-466. doi:10.1042/cs1030461. PMID 12401118. ABSTRACT READ IN FULL. Eight healthy males, GFR by 51Cr-EDTA, end-proximal fluid delivery by lithium clearance. PLACEBO ARM TAKEN: fractional excretion of lithium 26 +/- 2 percent, sodium/lithium clearance ratio 2.8 +/- 0.2 percent, fractional excretion of sodium 1.04 +/- 0.16 (control) and 0.70 +/- 0.07 (experimental).
notes: SOURCED IN HEALTHY HUMANS 2026-09-17 under nephron_segments_prereg.md, and the instrument is the point. The previous search for segmental handling looked for LITHIUM CLEARANCE IN DISEASE and for MICROPUNCTURE IN ANIMALS; this is lithium clearance in EIGHT HEALTHY MALES, which is the human measurement of end-proximal delivery and was there all along. || WHY LITHIUM MEASURES THIS: lithium is reabsorbed with sodium in the proximal tubule in proportion, and essentially not beyond it, so its fractional excretion is the fraction of filtered fluid delivered out of the proximal tubule. That is a METHODOLOGICAL assumption and not a measurement - it fails where distal lithium handling is altered, which is why the same paper warns that caffeine intake must be controlled when using the method. || THE PLACEBO ARM IS TAKEN, not the control period, because the paper's own internal consistency holds there: 0.26 x 0.028 = 0.73 percent against a measured fractional sodium excretion of 0.70. The control period gives 1.04 percent, which implies a distal escape near 4 percent. THE WITHIN-STUDY DRIFT IS REAL AND IS THE ROW'S UNCERTAINTY, not noise to be averaged away. || THIS IS NOT THE FRACTION RN.NA.MACULA_DENSA_FRACTION CARRIES. Lithium stops at the end of the proximal tubule; the macula densa sits at the end of the thick ascending limb, after the loop has taken most of what the proximal tubule passed on. 0.26 and 0.10 are different segments and both are real. || MEN ONLY, n = 8. || THE METHOD'S VALIDITY LIMITS ARE NOW ON THE ROW, AND THEY WERE MISSING. Atherton JC, Green R, Hughes S, McFall V, Sharples JA, Solomon LR, Wilson L. Lithium clearance in man: effects of dietary salt intake, acute changes in extracellular fluid volume, amiloride and frusemide. Clin Sci (Lond) 1987;73(6):645-651. doi:10.1042/cs0730645. PMID 3690979. ABSTRACT READ IN FULL. Normal human volunteers. Its conclusion, verbatim in substance: the lithium clearance method for assessment of proximal tubule salt and water reabsorption CAN be used with some degree of confidence at MEDIUM AND HIGH salt intake AND IN ACUTE VOLUME EXPANSION, but MAY NOT BE RELIABLE WHEN DIETARY SALT INTAKE IS LOW. Amiloride moved fractional lithium clearance on a low salt diet and was without effect at medium or high intake, which is the mechanism of the failure: a component of lithium is reabsorbed in the amiloride-sensitive distal nephron and that component only matters when distal sodium reabsorption is near-maximal. || SO THE ROW IS ADMISSIBLE AND ITS LOW-SODIUM EXTRAPOLATION IS NOT. Shirley's subjects sit at a fractional sodium excretion of 0.70-1.04 percent on an unrestricted intake, which is the regime Atherton certifies. A value read off a salt-depleted preparation would not be, and this model runs its salt step down to 38 mmol/day - BELOW that regime. NOTHING READS THIS ROW AS A FUNCTION OF INTAKE and it must not acquire such a reader without sourcing the intake dependence separately. || AND THE SAME GROUP PUBLISHED THE CAVEAT AGAINST ITS OWN INSTRUMENT, which is the reason to trust it: Shirley and Walter's own later work is what established the distal amiloride- and frusemide-sensitive component of lithium handling.
